****Role title: Credit Risk Analyst – FX Forwards****
Location: London
Hybrid / office-based: 3-in, 2-out.
3S Money is looking for a Credit Risk Analyst to support the development and ongoing management of its credit risk framework for clients using FX Forward products. This is an end-to-end credit risk role covering the assessment, approval and ongoing monitoring of clients that require credit exposure to undertake FX Forward transactions. The role will help establish a robust and proportionate credit risk framework, assess individual counterparties, set appropriate credit limits within delegated authority, monitor utilisation and exposure, and ensure that changes in client circumstances or risk are identified and acted upon promptly. The role reports to the Head of Risk and will work closely with FX Trading, Risk, Compliance and relevant commercial and operational teams.
****Our mission**** 3S Money is reinventing international business payments. Founded in 2018, our mission is to help growing businesses to send, receive and exchange money in over 190 countries. With offices in five countries and over 200 employees, you’ll be joining a high-energy, high-impact team that’s achieved profitability and has a wealth of opportunity ahead. ****Our culture**** At 3S Money, we believe in caring personally, staying curious and making an impact through collaboration not competition. Our culture is genuinely transparent with minimal hierarchy and a commitment to each employee’s professional growth. ****What you’ll be doing****
· Help develop and maintain the credit risk framework for FX Forward clients.
· Perform credit assessments for clients seeking access to FX Forward products.
· Review financial and other relevant information to assess creditworthiness and counterparty risk.
· Approve clients and set credit limits within delegated authority, escalating where required.
· Maintain and monitor the approved credit list, client limits, utilisation and exposures.
· Conduct ongoing and periodic reviews of approved clients.
· Identify and escalate limit breaches, deteriorating credit quality and material changes in risk.
· Recommend changes, reductions or withdrawal of limits where appropriate.
· Maintain clear records of credit assessments, decisions and approvals.
· Provide credit risk reporting and portfolio oversight to the Head of Risk.
****About you, you have****
· Experience in credit risk within financial services.
· Strong financial analysis and credit assessment skills.
· Experience setting credit limits and monitoring client exposures.
· FX or FX Forwards experience would be an advantage.
· Strong analytical skills and sound risk judgement.
· Able to make clear, independent and well-supported credit decisions.
****In return for your hard work:****
****💰**** Competitive Salary + plus stock options (after 12 months) & benefits
💻 Hybrid working setup in our wonderful city-centre office
📚 We foster non-BAU projects in our team, we want you to explore new avenues and expand your expertise to benefit your professional pathway & our teams.
➕ And much, much more....
****Our commitment to you****
****We are an equal opportunities employer.****
We make recruiting decisions based on your experience, skills and personality. Our passion and focus will always be to work with the best people. We’re creating services for everyone, so it’s imperative we work with everyone. Our diverse team has been the foundation to our success in building more efficient products, making better decisions and establishing an all-inclusive place to work. Applicants of all backgrounds are hugely encouraged to apply and discover the 3S way.

We can help monitor environments, observe borders, track natural disasters and connect unconnected communities.
Join us as we create a new domain of aerospace: Stratospace. You’ll be part of a highly-skilled, innovative and passionate group of people – Team AALTO. Together, we can Unlock Stratospace.

# Staff Tech Lead, Web & Developer Products
London, UK (Remote)
Our everyday digital experiences are in the middle of a realtime revolution: chatting alongside a livestream, getting realtime financial updates, or working with colleagues in a shared online space. Consumers now expect realtime as standard, and Ably powers a large part of it.
We put developers first. Our products help teams build, extend, and deliver realtime digital experiences, delivering over 700 billion messages to more than 2 billion devices every month. Teams at HubSpot, Fin, Dialpad, NASCAR, Sportsbet, and General Motors all build on Ably.
Working at Ably means helping build the infrastructure that will shape the next generation of the internet. More of what people do online is becoming live, shared and interactive, which only makes what we build more relevant and more necessary. AI is the latest place that shows up. There's still so much to build, and we'd like your help with it.
## **About this role**
As the Staff Tech Lead for the Developer Experience team at Ably, you’ll report directly to our CTO and co-own the DevEx vision and strategy. You’ll lead the engineering team that owns our customer-facing web platform - our dashboard, documentation platform, and control plane - transforming it into a world-class experience for our users.
You are a senior, hands-on engineer who’s passionate about building for developers like yourself; someone who’ll obsess over the developer journey and elevate the user experience of the Ably platform. You’ll blend deep full-stack expertise with a strong product mindset, and lead a team of engineers working on initiatives where the feedback loop is immediate, because you and your team are the target users of the very ecosystem you are building.
Ably is an AI-forward organisation and this is a leadership role for an AI-first engineer. You must have confident, hands-on experience of AI-assisted development and be able to define how a team actually works with these tools day to day, and tell the difference between genuine leverage and noise.
## **Day to day you will**
* **Obsess over developer experience.** You’ll have broad responsibility for elevating how developers interact with Ably’s platform and services, partnering with the DevEx PM as a unified leadership team to deliver a developer experience that becomes a reference point for the industry.
* **Define and lead on AI-first working practices.** You’ll be the catalyst and standard-setter for AI-enabled development across the team. You’ll leverage LLMs and AI tools to accelerate velocity, design workflows, set the guardrails and coach engineers to use them well - without compromising on engineering integrity.
* **Lead technical execution and vision.** You’ll lead a team of five engineers building customer-facing web applications and own the technical architecture and design decisions for our dashboard, docs platform, marketing website, and billing UI.

# Aon Graduate Programme 2027 - Commercial Risk Consulting
**Commercial Risk Consulting - Graduate Programme 2027**
**Start Date** 1st September 2027
**Application closing date** 7th December 2026 *Please note, we may close earlier if we receive the quantity, quality & diversity of applications required.*
**Better Decisions Begin with You**
At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organisation, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.
**Launch Your Career in Commercial Risk Consulting**
Join Aon as a Commercial Risk Consulting graduate and, from day one, you’ll be an integral part of either our Strategic Engagement (Inpoint) or Aon M&A and Transaction Solutions (AMATS) team. You’ll help clients navigate complex business challenges, handle risk and make better-informed decisions.
**Strategic Engagement (Inpoint):**
Inpoint is Aon’s carrier engagement and management business, working primarily with insurers across Commercial Risk. Our teams use market insight, portfolio analytics and Aon’s broader capabilities to build stronger, more strategic relationships with carrier partners.
Strategic Engagement is focused on helping Aon and its carrier partners identify shared priorities, understand portfolio performance and turn insight into meaningful action. This is not a traditional strategy consulting role. It is a relationship-led, data-informed opportunity at the centre of Aon’s engagement with the insurance market.
As a Strategic Engagement Graduate, you will work with colleagues across Strategy & Technology Group (STG), the Global Broking Centre (GBC) and Commercial Risk UK. You will help prepare insight for senior conversations with insurers, support engagement on portfolio opportunities and contribute to initiatives that strengthen how Aon and its carrier partners work together.
The role offers exposure to senior leaders across Aon and the insurance market. It also provides the chance to build a strong understanding of commercial insurance, carrier priorities, broking, and portfolio dynamics.
**What You Will Do**
* **Analyse market, carrier and portfolio information** to identify trends and opportunities, turning data and analytics into practical insights for carrier and internal partners discussions
* **Support strategic relationship planning and engagement** for key insurers, helping teams establish clear priorities, actions and follow-through while deepening your knowledge of customer relationship management
* **Collaborate across Inpoint, GBC and Commercial Risk UK** to understand carrier objectives, capture insight and coordinate engagement with the market, building your project management and consulting skills over time
* **Contribute to strategic carrier meetings and senior collaborator discussions** and learn how strong commercial relationships are developed throughout Aon and the insurance sector
* **Prepare clear, high-quality materials and presentations** for strategic meetings and portfolio reviews, using focused research and document review to communicate complex information concisely
**Aon M&A and Transaction Solutions (AMATS):**
Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) and other event-driven situations can be complex, time-critical and highly specialised. The AMATS team typically assists clients in three core areas, prior to, during and/or after completion of an M&A deal or other investment opportunity, by:
* Providing due diligence on an ‘target’ business across a wide range of deal-critical areas, including risk & insurance, cyber & digital, human capital and climate maters. This diligence evaluates the target’s risk exposures - past, current, and future - which may impact transaction value for the buyer
* Arranging insurance solutions aimed at de-risking transaction liabilities and enhancing investor returns, often removing deal-breaking risks. This involves structuring and placing solutions like warranty & indemnity insurance and using insurance capital to mitigate contingent risks, such as tax and litigation
* Delivering portfolio value creation programmes for financial sponsors, including private equity, infrastructure funds, and real estate investors. Use their portfolio scale and insights from analysis. Coordinate efforts to reduce the total cost of risk and improve governance
The clients include financial sponsors and Corporates, with transaction sizes ranging from small UK domestic deals (such as Voyage Care’s acquisition of Orchard Healthcare) to some of the largest cross-border transactions (such as KONE’s $34.4 billion combination with TK Elevators). Further deal examples can be found on Aon’s LinkedIn page.
You’ll gain exposure to several parts of our transaction advisory and broking business to help build your understanding of why clients implement M&A deals and how Aon supports their business and investment objectives.
**What You Will Do**
* **Support transaction advisory work** for private equity, infrastructure, real estate and corporate clients, helping the team research and analyse risks connected with M&A deals
* **Support the arrangement of M&A insurance solutions** by helping colleagues prepare information for the insurance market and learning how transaction risks can be transferred
* **Coordinate Aon expertise across practices and geographies** while developing your internal network and learning to handle actions and workstreams across a fast-moving transaction process
* **Help identify relevant Aon products, services and solutions** that may support client deal and investment objectives, applying commercial judgement and broader business context
* **Build strong collaborative connections** with clients, insurers, M&A advisers and internal collaborators, while developing your consulting and business communication skills over time
**Your Development**

# Retention Manager (CRM & Lifecycle)
* £40,000 - £55,000 per year
* Marketing
## Job description
**Revenue team · Reports to the Head of Revenue · Remote first**
**The role**
Arc makes precision engineered aluminium and titanium cases for the devices people use most, sold as an object rather than an accessory. The business has grown quickly on one hero product, trades worldwide with the US and UK as its core markets, and has built a large and growing customer base along the way.
That customer base is the opportunity. Arc has invested heavily in acquiring customers and comparatively little in developing them, which means there is substantial untapped value in people who already own and like the product. The platform, the agency support and the data are in place. What comes next is the programme that makes the most of them: sharper segmentation, a lifecycle built around how customers actually buy, and a loyalty proposition that suits a considered, upgrade driven purchase.
This is a build role, and a commercially significant one. Improvement here falls through to profit without media cost attached, which makes retention the one lever that strengthens acquisition economics and revenue at the same time. You will be hands on, you will make the case for investment, and you will have room to build it your way.
**What you are accountable for**
* **Developing customers beyond a first purchase:** growing the proportion who return, and the value they bring when they do.
* **Revenue generated through owned channels:** email, SMS, loyalty and any channel added over time, and their contribution to the overall number.
* **The customer database as a commercial asset:** its structure, accuracy, health and usefulness to the wider team.
* **The lifecycle experience after purchase:** everything between the order confirmation and the next purchase.
* **Customer understanding:** being the person who understands the customer best, and making sure the rest of the business benefits from it.
* **The contribution of our CRM partner:** the output we get, the value we receive, and how the relationship develops.
**What you own**
**Lifecycle strategy and roadmap**
* The retention plan, its sequencing, and the case for what gets built first
* The flow architecture end to end: welcome, browse and basket recovery, post purchase, fitting and care, upgrade moments, replenishment and back in stock
* The campaign calendar, and how it maps to the trading year and to product launches
* Identifying the moments that matter commercially and building around them, rather than sending to a fixed schedule
**Segmentation and customer data**
* Developing the segmentation model around behaviour and value, building on what exists today
* Identifying high value customers early and treating them accordingly
* Recognising that customers return for different reasons, and tailoring programmes to each
* List health: growth, engagement, suppression and consent across markets
* Making the database genuinely useful to the acquisition side for audience building and exclusion
**Owned channels: email, SMS and beyond**
* Strategy, calendar, briefing and final approval on what goes out
* Campaign programming: the mix of brand, product, launch and promotional sends, and the frequency the audience will bear
* Deliverability and sender reputation
* The testing programme across subject lines, creative, offer and timing
* Platform configuration, and getting the most from the current stack
* Growing the channel mix over time. SMS is the immediate opportunity, with direct mail and other owned channels worth evaluating where the price point and the customer justify them
**Reactivation and lapsed customers**
* The lapsed customer strategy, including how lapse is defined by behaviour rather than by a fixed window
* Win back programmes, and the judgement on which customers are worth reactivating and at what cost
* Testing reactivation offers against holdouts, so the true cost of winning someone back is known rather than assumed
* A sunset policy, so that attention and spend concentrate where there is a realistic prospect of return
**Voice of the customer**
* Owning customer feedback loops: reviews, surveys, post purchase responses and recurring support themes
* Working closely with customer support, who own the queue, to turn what customers actually ask and complain about into briefs for the site, the product pages, the lifecycle programme and the product roadmap
* Keeping segments and personas alive as working tools rather than a one off exercise
* Being the voice of the customer in trading and planning conversations, and bringing evidence rather than opinion
**Agency direction**
* Reviewing what is live, forming an independent view, and setting the roadmap from there
* The brief, the targets and the review rhythm
* Assessing value delivered and guiding how the partnership develops
**Offer and lifecycle promotions**
* When an offer is used, at what level and for whom
* Protecting margin by reserving incentives for customers who genuinely need them
* Agreeing policy with the Head of Revenue and holding to it
**Loyalty**
* Designing a proposition suited to a considered, upgrade driven purchase rather than a generic points scheme
* Evaluating and selecting a platform where one is needed
* Launch, adoption and ongoing management
**Cross sell and lifecycle merchandising**
* Growing the number of customers who buy more than one product, led by lifecycle rather than discount
* Post purchase and accessory sequences, and the timing of them
* Working with the brand and product side on what is promoted and when
**Post purchase experience and foundations**
* The full sequence: confirmation, dispatch, arrival, fitting and care, review request and follow on
* Working with brand and operations so the unboxing and follow up match the price point
* Integrations between the ecommerce platform, CRM, advertising platforms and the support desk, so reporting can be trusted
**Where this role starts and stops**
This role owns the customer database and the lifecycle after purchase. The Acquisition Manager owns the journey up to and including the first purchase, and the website that carries it, because the majority of Arc's traffic is new to the brand and site conversion is an acquisition measure. Where the two meet:
* **Email and SMS capture on site:** you own the mechanic and the offer. Acquisition owns placement and its effect on conversion.
* **Audiences built from customer data:** you own the segments. Acquisition owns how they are applied in platform.
* **Paid activity aimed at existing customers:** Acquisition executes it, measured jointly with you on repeat revenue.
* **Pages for returning and logged in customers:** you brief the requirement. Acquisition owns the roadmap and build priority.
* **Promotional offers:** you own lifecycle offers. Acquisition owns acquisition offers. Policy is set with the Head of Revenue.
* **Customer feedback and support themes:** customer support owns the queue and the response. You own the insight and what the business does with it.
Crossover is expected and healthy. Where ownership is not obvious, the test is simple: which measure moves if this works, and who is accountable for it. The Head of Revenue settles anything genuinely ambiguous.
**Working with our agency partner**
* **Partner:** campaign and flow build. **You:** strategy, and the roadmap the build serves.
* **Partner:** design and deployment. **You:** briefing, approval and quality control.
* **Partner:** platform reporting. **You:** deciding what is measured and what good looks like.
* **Partner:** executing the calendar. **You:** owning the calendar and what belongs on it.
* **Partner:** recommending tactics. **You:** judging which tactics fit the brand and the margin.
**How the role is measured**
Targets are set with the Head of Revenue and reviewed quarterly.
* Repeat customer rate
* Repeat purchases as a share of total revenue
* Revenue and gross profit per acquired customer over twelve months
* Owned channel share of sessions and of revenue
* Split between automated flow revenue and campaign revenue
* Reactivation rate of lapsed customers, and the cost of achieving it
* Discount rate applied to repeat orders
* Cross sell rate, and average order value on multi product orders
* Time between first and second purchase
* Engaged list size and growth, alongside deliverability health
* Loyalty enrolment and participation, once live
* Review volume and rating trend, and customer insight translated into action elsewhere in the business
**Practical terms**
* **Reporting line:** Head of Revenue
* **Level:** Manager, with a clear route to Head of as the channel and team grow
* **Location:** Remote first. UK or European time zones, with a quarterly in person meet up
* **Team:** Agency partners from the outset, with additional headcount planned as the channel matures
* **Salary:** £40,000 to £55,000 base salary, dependent on experience
## Job requirements
**The calibre we are looking for**
* Has owned a CRM platform hands on, personally building flows and segments rather than briefing others to do it
* Has developed a retention programme from an early stage rather than only maintaining a mature one. The first year here is about building
* Comfortable with cohort and lifetime value analysis. Can read a repeat purchase curve, size the opportunity and argue for the investment
* Commercially minded about promotions, and able to judge when an incentive is genuinely earning its cost
* A self starter who is comfortable building process in a small, fast moving team
**Useful, but not essential**
* Launched a loyalty programme
* SMS as well as email, or offline channels such as direct mail
* Premium or considered purchase categories
* Products tied to a replacement or upgrade cycle
* Running customer research, surveys or structured feedback programmes
* Experience of a CRM platform migration

### About Arondite
Arondite enables organisations to wield autonomy, data and AI at scale. We equip operators with the foundational software to orchestrate their mix of platforms and capabilities and take mission-critical decisions faster than their adversaries.
We exist to ensure the UK and its allies out-think, out-pace and out-adapt those who seek to threaten our values and way of life. Our technology is designed for deployment in the world’s most austere environments, and is relied upon by the world’s most demanding operators. We deploy alongside them, bringing our technical expertise wherever it is needed.
**You will join Arondite at a pivotal moment in the company’s journey.** We are ambitious, building for the long-term and backed by globally renowned investors including Index Ventures (Anthropic, Wiz, Figma, Revolut). Our company is being built by exceptional people; people who find high-tempo and challenging work engaging and exciting and who consistently deliver outsized impact.
**You will have ownership and autonomy from Day One.** There is no corporate ladder at Arondite. We hire the best people and give them extremely high levels of autonomy; the sky is the limit for an individual with the right ambition.
If you are motivated by our mission and if you want to be part of an outstanding team, then we want to hear from you.
### Role overview
You will own how our customers across the world understand Cobalt. That means what it is, what it does, how it is built, how it is deployed, and the value it can bring to mission-critical enterprise challenges.
You will sit at the centre of our go-to-market, working between Marketing & Communications, Business Development and Product. You will turn a deep, modular platform into clear compelling win themes, sharp collateral and confident GTM teams. You will define where we aim and how we win in each segment. You will help ensure every customer conversation our BD and deployed teams are clear, credible and compelling.
You'll join a lean MarComms team that is scaling fast. There's no product marketing playbook to inherit: you'll write it, then build the machine that runs it. You'll also stay hands-on, writing decks and briefings yourself, working with engineers to understand the architecture, and joining customer conversations to hear what lands. We'll judge your success by pipeline and win rates, not by the volume of collateral.
### What you will do:
* **Segment go-to-market strategy.** For each segment and campaign, define how we win: the buyers and influencers we target, from operators to CIOs, the channels and routes to market that reach them, the value propositions that land, and the competitive win themes that set us apart in highly competitive technology landscapes.
* **Positioning, messaging and naming.** Own the single source of truth for how we describe Cobalt: its capabilities, features, architecture, use cases and deployment profiles. Name and package those capabilities into solutions for each segment.
* **The go-to-market content library.** In partnership with Content Strategy and Marketing colleagues, build and maintain the suite of decks, capability briefings, fact sheets and use-case narratives our teams use every day, plus the value and ROI tools that help buyers build a business case.
* **Launches, campaigns and partners.** Position and launch each release with Product, and turn segment strategy into campaigns with MarComms. Build the partner marketing programme that brings our hardware, model and integration partners into the Cobalt story.
* **Market insight, enablement and proof.** Run competitive intelligence and win/loss analysis, and equip BD and deployment teams with the information they need to win. Turn deployments into case studies with our deployment strategists, and provide the product and technical point of view behind our thought leadership
## Requirements
*Arondite aims to bring together individuals from diverse backgrounds and with different perspectives; we therefore don’t expect people to have experience across every area of the requirements. Please apply even if you only partially fulfil the following lists.*
### You should have
* Extensive experience in product marketing, technical marketing or a related role, including building go-to-market strategies and campaigns for distinct customer segments buying complex software.
* Experience positioning to senior enterprise buyers, including value and ROI messaging for CIOs, COOs and operational leaders.
* The technical fluency to understand data integration, AI models, sensors and edge deployment, and to explain them accurately to non-technical buyers.
* Excellent writing and storytelling, and a track record of influencing Product and sales teams without formal authority.
### Ideally you will also have:
* Experience in defence, national security, critical national infrastructure or another regulated enterprise sector.
* Experience as an early Product Marketing hire would be highly advantageous, establishing the function as an IC in a rapidly scaling organisation with minimal structure and frequent ambiguity.
* Time at a platform company with a forward-deployed engineering model.
* Experience positioning one platform across several industries, including naming and packaging vertical solutions.
* Experience building partner programmes or partner-led routes to market, through systems integrators, primes or technology alliances.
* Eligibility for UK Security Check (SC) clearance.
### Right to Work
We require that all candidates have an existing Right to Work in the UK at the time of application.
### Security clearance
We believe in working closely with defence customers. As a result, this role is likely to require you to hold a clearance or be willing to undergo UK security vetting to Security Check (SC) or above. This normally requires having continuous residency in the UK for at least 5 years.

Available Locations: London, UK

Engineering Manager, Agentic Discovery

About the Department

Emerging Technologies & Incubation (ETI) is where new and bold products are built and released within Cloudflare. Rather than being constrained by the structures which make Cloudflare a hugely successful business, we are able to leverage them to deliver entirely new tools and products to our customers. Cloudflare’s edge and network make it possible to solve problems at massive scale and efficiency which would be impossible for almost any other organization.

About the Team

We build the products that enable the next era of the Internet: making domains Readable, Discoverable, and Callable for autonomous AI agents.

 

Here at Cloudflare, agentic discovery is a core part of our vision for the Agentic Internet. As AI agents change how humans and machines find, evaluate, and act on information, businesses need tools to control how they are represented and reached. We build capabilities that enable website owners to prepare their sites for agent interaction, test and observe how agents read their content, establish open interaction standards (like WebMCP), and create entirely new channels to reach agentic audiences.

 

We are a tight-knit group that communicates and collaborates regularly. We celebrate our achievements, support each other when we make mistakes, and hold each other and our work to a high standard.

About the Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to build and lead the engineering team across our Agentic Discovery portfolio.

 

You will be responsible for the people, execution, and engineering quality behind customer-facing products that help businesses manage how AI agents understand, represent, and interact with their digital properties. You will partner closely with Product Management and engineering teams across Cloudflare to shape priorities around Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), content ingestion/indexing, agent observation and testing tools, and open tool-execution standards (such as WebMCP and Generative UI).

 

This is a management role for someone who is deeply technically credible. You will not be expected to write most of the code, but you should be able to understand the systems your engineers operate, challenge architectural decisions around distributed systems and web-scale data pipelines, ask the right questions when something is going wrong, and step into a technical problem when the situation calls for it.

 

At the same time, we are looking for a manager, not a tech lead with direct reports. Your success will be measured by the quality and output of the team you build, the engineers you develop, and the systems and products they deliver.

 

This role may require flexibility to be on-call outside of standard working hours to address technical issues as needed.

  • Manage, coach, and grow engineers working across customer-facing Agentic Discovery products, AEO tooling, and agent-web interaction standards.
  • Own execution by establishing clear priorities, creating predictable delivery, and giving engineers the context and autonomy to own meaningful areas of the product.
  • Lead the development of tools enabling Cloudflare customers to make their content Readable (structured content transformation), Discoverable (indexing, directories, and AEO), and Callable (WebMCP, APIs, Generative UI) for autonomous agents.
  • Build tools for customers to test, observe, measure, and control how AI agents find and interact with their websites and applications.
  • Partner closely with Product Management to understand customer problems, shape the roadmap, and turn broad opportunities into clear engineering outcomes.
  • Identify how Cloudflare's global network and edge signals can enable unique products that help businesses reach trusted agentic audiences at scale.
  • Balance near-term product delivery with thoughtful technical investments that allow promising ideas to grow.
  • Own the operational health of the systems in your area, including observability, incident response, data quality, and long-term reliability.
  • Develop technical leaders and create space for engineers to lead architecture and implementation.

Responsibilities

We want you to love it here. This role is a great fit for you if:

 

  • You have led and developed a high-performing engineering team(s) and can point to what that team shipped and how the people on it grew.
  • You are technically credible with experienced engineers. You can review a design, understand the trade-offs in distributed systems or web-scale data pipelines, and recognize when a technical problem needs deeper investigation.
  • You are comfortable managing a team working across several related technical areas (such as search/indexing, protocol standards, and UI engineering) and can create clarity without requiring every problem to fit neatly into a single box.
  • You care deeply about reliability and quality, particularly when the output of a system is data that users and AI agents rely on to navigate the Internet.
  • You have strong product judgment and enjoy working with Product Management to decide what is worth building, what needs improvement, and what should not be built at all.
  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and with finding structure in areas where the opportunity is clearer than the roadmap.
  • You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, and can explain complex technical decisions to both engineers and non-engineers.

Examples of Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience

  • Strong technical grounding in distributed systems, web-scale data platforms, agentic architectures, Internet infrastructure, or adjacent areas.
  • Experience building customer-facing products involving content indexing, crawling, analytics, or complex user interaction patterns.
  • Experience operating systems where correctness, data quality, and reliability matter as much as feature delivery.

  • Experience partnering closely with Product Management to shape and execute a roadmap.

Bonus Points

  • Experience working with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platforms, search/indexing, or testing and observability platforms.
  • Experience turning complex underlying internet systems or data into intuitive, high-value products for a broad audience.

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

**About Us**
Axelera AI is not your regular deep-tech company. We are creating the next-generation AI platform to support anyone who wants to help advancing humanity and improve the world around us.

**Position Overview**
As a Staff AI Application Engineer in the Model Enablement team (Application Software), you will build our model enablement platform and decide how each model runs across the Metis or Europa AIPU, the host CPU and the host's accelerators. How this work is split and scheduled determines most of the end-to-end performance a customer sees in the Voyager SDK.
The role combines architecture and hands-on work across the model frontend, the graph compiler, the runtime and the application pipeline. During model bring-up, you cover the frontend and graph side, and a device-side engineer covers the backend.
Our team uses AI coding agents in daily work, and you will use them to build, test and verify your own work. We also welcome experienced field application engineers, technical leads and engineering managers who want to return to hands-on engineering. Experience in planning, delegating and reviewing work transfers well to working with AI agents.
**Key responsibilities:**
* **Model enablement platform and agent harness:** Build the platform that engineers and AI agents use to bring up models: reusable tools to partition, compile, run and profile; environments with access to real hardware; closed-loop runs that apply a change, measure it against the reference and repeat; and verification (differential testing, regression detection) integrated into CI.
* **Model ingestion:** Own how a PyTorch or ONNX model is captured, analysed and split across the AIPU's matrix and RISC-V vector units, the host CPU and the host's accelerators (GPU, NPU, video decoder), with placement tags that users can read and override. Build this with the graph compiler team so it works for every model.
* **Heterogeneous execution:** Extend that split to large models, cascades and multi-model pipelines, for example with expert offloading and caching across device and host memory. Agree the plan with the graph compiler team.
* **End-to-end performance:** With the application team (pipeline builder) and the runtime team, bring each model to its best end-to-end performance: overlap of host and device work, zero-copy buffers, batching, multi-core scheduling, and models with several inputs. * Daily use of AI coding agents on real engineering work, with the judgment to review and test their output.

* Hands-on experience with MLIR or another compiler framework (TVM, XLA, TorchInductor, IREE).
* Experience with an inference runtime or execution engine (ONNX Runtime execution providers, a custom NPU or DSP runtime).
* Experience with GPU compute (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan) or SIMD optimization on Arm or x86.

We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand.

# Independent Member, Financial Markets Infrastructure Committee (FMIC)
London, United Kingdom
## Job Description
**Introduction**
The Bank of England’s Court of Directors is seeking to appoint a new independent member to the Financial Market Infrastructure Committee (FMIC).
The Bank of England sits at the heart of the UK’s economy and financial system. Its mission is to promote the good of the people of the United Kingdom by maintaining monetary and financial stability.
The FMIC was established as a statutory committee of the Bank under the Bank of England Act 1998 (as amended by the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023). The FMIC governs the work of the Bank of England on financial market infrastructure encompassing supervision and policy for payment systems (including stablecoin), central counterparties and central securities depositories. Its decisions play a crucial role in ensuring the resilience of the systems and markets on which both retail and wholesale users depend. This is a particularly interesting time given the extent of technological change and innovation taking place across the FMI landscape and a unique opportunity to play a part in a once-in-a-generation modernisation of money and markets. For more information on the FMIC’s work, see our most recent annual report available here (see here).
The coming period will see the FMIC – along with the Bank’s other policy committees – continue to deal with a wide range of issues. This will include assessing financial and operational risks to the resilience of FMIs and ensuring the Bank’s approach to supervision remains appropriate to the evolving market context. The Committee will continue to embed the new responsibilities of the Bank in relation to rulemaking and the secondary innovation objective through which the Bank seeks to facilitate innovation in the provision of FMI services.
The knowledge and analytical rigour that the independent members bring to bear on the Committee’s work, along with the challenge they provide, ensures that the FMIC’s decision making is robust and effective.
**Appointment description**
Key responsibilities of FMIC Members
• Providing independent challenge, perspective and insights across the breadth of the FMIC’s policymaking and supervisory remit.
• Contributing an understanding of the broader context to FMIC discussions.
• Providing oversight of the FMIC’s strategy and delivery.
**Organisation description**
The FMIC is accountable to Parliament and reports to it annually. The FMIC has several non-delegable responsibilities which include the Bank’s FMI related policy-making functions.
FMIC is chaired by the Governor or Deputy Governor for Financial Stability. Its other members consist of 4 Bank members (including the Bank’s Executive Director for FMI), and at least 3 (currently 4) independent members. The Committee meets regularly to take decisions on rules and on firm-specific issues. In addition, it sets the strategy and approach to supervision.
**Minimum criteria**
* **Strong and proven financial sector knowledge and experience at a senior level**– candidates must have the experience necessary to make independent decisions. They must demonstrate that they have used their financial sector expertise operating at a senior level in or in relation to financial services organisations, ideally financial market infrastructure firms.
**Essential criteria**
* **Decision-making skills** – the FMIC makes decisions that directly affect firms and people. All members should have strong leadership skills, a strategic mindset, and be ready to take tough decisions and stand by them.
* **Analytical ability**– candidates will need to be able to absorb large volumes of complex information and reach reasoned and robust conclusions.
* **Independence of thought and interpersonal skills** – Candidates must be able to exert influence within the FMIC providing robust challenge whilst working closely and constructively with FMIC members.
* **Excellent communication skills**– the Bank has to communicate with firms, trade associations, civil society, ministers and relevant Parliamentary Committees. External members of the Committee can be called before the Treasury Committee in the Commons and the Financial Services Regulation Committee in the Lords (along with other members) to explain the FMIC’s policies.
* **Undisputed integrity and standing** – candidates should have no reservations about meeting the requirements of the Bank’s Code of Conduct and the Conflicts Code for the FMIC. An assessment of potential conflicts of interest will be undertaken as part of the selection process.
**Desirable criteria**
* An understanding of how regulation can enable responsible innovation and/or influence regulatory approaches in other jurisdictions.
* An understanding of how financial infrastructure firms effectively implement and maintain technology infrastructure, and the opportunities and risks that technological developments may pose for the industry and regulators.
* An understanding of how policy is developed and implemented, including the theory of regulation.
**Appointment terms**
Members will normally be appointed for a fixed term of 3years. Members may typically serve no more than 2consecutive terms. Members will ultimately be accountable to Court.
**Conflicts of interest**
Members will be subject to FMIC’sconflicts-of-interest policy. Applicants must declare any actual or potential conflicts before appointment and any conflicts that arise during their term. Candidates should therefore consider carefully whether their existing appointments, responsibilities or interests could affect, or reasonably be perceived to affect, their ability to serve on the committee.
**Time commitment and remuneration**
The anticipated commitment is 30days**.** The pay rate for the role is £31,500 per annum and reasonable expenses will be paid in accordance with Bank policies.
**Diversity and equality of opportunity**
The Bank of England values and promotes diversity and is committed to equality of opportunity.
We believe that drawing on different perspectives, backgrounds and experiences supports effective decision-making and better outcomes for the public. Appointments will be made on merit following a fair and open process.
**How to apply**
Interested candidates should submit their application by completing the application form including the application questions and uploading their CV.
Closing date is **16 November 2026 at 23:59**
**Our Approach to Inclusion**
The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve.
At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public.
Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme. If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application.
**Security Vetting Process**
Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice.
The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis.
## About Us
We are the UK's central bank - and we are a bank like no other; known by our peers for our world-leading thinking on policy and strategy.
Our mission is to promote the good of the people of the UK by maintaining monetary and financial stability. We seek to keep prices stable and people's money safe. We know our work matters to people, to families, up and down the UK. We are driven by curiosity and the desire to do important, challenging work.
It takes a great team to run the Bank of England. We rely on each other to play our part. We benefit from a collaborative culture and long-established flexible ways of working, supporting our colleagues balance their work and personal lives. We strive to be a place where people feel they belong and have equal access to opportunities, because different perspectives helps us make the best decisions for the public.
There's much to gain from working with us - from career defining work at the heart of the UK economy, being part of a fantastic team, and a rewarding compensation package.
**Join us and find a bank like no other. Together, we can make a difference.**
The Bank of England will use and protect the information you provide when you apply for a role with us, in line with our obligations under data protection law. This is so we can assess your suitability for the role and administer your application. If you’re successful we’ll use it to offer you a position and onboard you to join the Bank.

Central to this is publishing our journalism with speed, accuracy and authority. You’ll play a pivotal role in shaping how BBC News appears on platforms like YouTube, Instagram and TikTok. You’ll ensure our output is accurate, engaging and optimised for digital‐first consumption.
You’ll work closely with teams in the BBC Newsroom covering some of the biggest stories of our time, from breaking news to global conflicts and deep investigations and bring their reporting to life in ways that connect with digital-first audiences.
This is your chance to help shape how BBC News shows up on social: bold, fast, creative, distinctive, and relentlessly audience‐first.
**WHY JOIN THE TEAM**
BBC News is supercharging our social and off‐platform strategy, with a clear mission to meet audiences where they are; particularly those who don’t have a regular connection with the BBC or News. You’ll join at a pivotal moment, shaping how BBC News looks, sounds and behaves on social platforms; championing innovation and strengthening trust. We have huge ambition to broaden and grow our activity on social in the pursuit of truth with no agenda, delivering high quality news to educate and inform audiences.
**YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES & IMPACT**
* Oversee high-quality weekend social publishing across BBC News platforms, ensuring all content meets editorial standards and delivers impact during major news moments
* Edit, sub and optimise scripts, headlines, copy, thumbnails and visual treatments to maximise accuracy, clarity and platform-specific performance
* Collaborate with correspondents and reporters to develop innovative social-first treatments of BBC journalism informed by audience insight, data and social listening
* Produce, shape and edit world-class social video and visual news content
* Coordinate daily social workflows, supporting colleagues and maintaining fast, accurate publishing during breaking news situations
* Contribute to editorial planning by identifying opportunities for distinctive coverage across UK, political and international news stories
* Play a central role in our weekend coverage, balancing speed, accuracy and editorial judgement to maintain audience trust in fast-moving situations
**YOUR KEY SKILLS & EXPERIENCE**
**Essential Criteria**
* Proven ability to create, write, sub and publish news across major social platforms in all formats, with a strong eye for accuracy, tone and platform nuance
* Strong editorial judgement and experience covering breaking news at national or international level, with confidence making real-time editorial decisions
* Collaborative and calm under pressure, able to work across teams, maintain high standards and provide constructive feedback
* Proficient in tools like Final Cut Pro and Photoshop, with experience overseeing the full production cycle of social or digital video news content
* Deep understanding of social audience behaviour, including content discovery, moderation and sharing, and the ability to turn insight into recommendations and new ideas
* Comfortable using analytics tools to interpret performance data, identify patterns and inform both daily decisions and longer-term strategy
* Keen understanding of news consumption trends on social media platforms

# Retail Committee and Remuneration & People Committee member
### Posted on 28/10/2026
* ## The opportunity
* For more than 60 years, British Heart Foundation (BHF) has been at the forefront of cutting-edge research to save and improve millions of lives. Despite the progress we’ve made, our work has never been more needed; heart and circulatory diseases remain the biggest killers globally, with millions of people living with these conditions today in the United Kingdom alone. Our lifesaving work is primarily advanced through long-term investment in medical research, and we currently have over £460 million of BHF-funded research underway, funding more than 700 active research projects. Powered by an incredible team of volunteers, colleagues, supporters, partners, and scientists, we are more ambitious and determined than ever with potential cures and treatments we need now in sight. Our vision is a world where everyone has a healthier heart for longer, and our pioneering research transforms the lives of millions of people in the UK and across the world. A leading independent funder of research into heart and circulatory diseases, we are the UK’s largest charity retailer with around 650 stores, an employee base of over 4,000, supported by a further 20,000 volunteers. We are now seeking an exceptional individual to join our Retail Committee and Remuneration & People Committee. This joint role reflects the vital relationship between our retail and people priorities. As a member of both Committees, you’ll help ensure that our retail transformation, people strategy and organisational development remain aligned to BHF's mission and long-term ambitions. **To succeed in this role, you’ll:**
+ Bring substantial current or recent senior-level experience within a retail organisation, with direct insight into retail strategy, operations, customer trends and the wider retail landscape.
+ Have significant executive-level accountability for people, culture, organisational change and workforce strategy, ideally within a large and complex organisation.
+ A strong track record of shaping and leading workforce strategy, organisational and transformational change, culture, talent, reward, employee relations, equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI), and employee engagement, ideally across a large and dispersed workforce
+ Relevant experience in a substantial retail or consumer-facing organisation, with an understanding of the people implications of commercial strategy and operational deliveryAble to contribute strategically and constructively, offering independent insight and challenge in a non-executive committee environment, you’ll share our commitment to BHF’s mission and values and bring the passion and expertise to help us transform even more lives.
**How to apply**The British Heart Foundation is partnering with Nurole, to find our new committee member for our Retail and People committees. You can find out more and apply here. To arrange an informal conversation or in case of any other queries, please contact joshua.dernie@nurole.com **Interview process**Interviews will be held via MS Teams.
+ 1st stage interviews will be held 4th December 2026
+ 2nd stage interviews will be held 14th December 2026
**Terms of appointment**
+ This is a voluntary role, but reasonable expenses will be met.
+ The appointment is for an initial three-year term, renewable for a second term, subject to approval and continued contribution.
+ The Retail Committee meets four times per year: two full-day in-person meetings (March and September) and two three-hour online meetings (June and December)
+ The Remuneration & People Committee normally meets twice per year, with meetings generally lasting two to three hours
+ Overall expected commitment of approximately 1–2 days per quarter.
+ Members are expected to prepare thoroughly for discussions, take part in induction and keep up to date with developments across BHF Retail and the wider people agenda

# Employee Relations Specialist – Change Projects
### Posted on 28/10/2026
* ## The opportunity
* We’re looking
for an experienced Employee Relations specialist to join us on a 12-month fixed-term
contract and play a pivotal role in supporting organisational change. You’ll
use your expertise to shape and deliver change effectively, enabling British
Heart Foundation (BHF) to continue its mission of helping people have a
healthier heart for longer.
You’ll work with managers and People colleagues to plan and support fair,
meaningful and legally compliant change processes, including restructures, role
changes and individual and collective redundancy consultations. You’ll provide
pragmatic specialist advice, identify and manage employment law and employee
relations risks, and help ensure each project is delivered consistently,
sensitively and to agreed timescales. Alongside this project work, you’ll support a proportionate portfolio of
complex ER casework in line with the People Relations Job Description. Acting
as an escalation point from our People Operations team, you’ll advise managers
on issues such as conduct, capability, grievance, attendance and
discrimination, taking ownership of cases where required and escalating
significant risks or concerns.
**About you**
As our ideal candidate, you’ll be an experienced Employee Relations (ER) professional
with substantial hands-on experience of delivering organisational change and
redundancy programmes and projects, alongside a strong track record in complex
ER casework.
CIPD Level 5 qualified,
you’ll have up-to-date knowledge of UK employment law, the Equality Act, ACAS
Code of Conduct and employee relations best practice. You’ll have a strong
understanding of organisational change, and individual and collective
redundancy, including consultation, fair selection, suitable alternative
employment and legal risk.
You’ll have
significant experience of applying this expertise to provide clear, pragmatic
advice and influence key stakeholders through sensitive complex decisions and
situations.
You’ll also
bring experience of:
+ delivering organisational change
and redundancy programmes, including consultation and applying relevant
legal frameworks
+ managing multiple change
workstreams, milestones and deadlines
+ partnering confidently with senior
leaders, managers, People teams and employee representatives
+ providing clear, pragmatic advice
on complex ER cases and issues
+ takening ownership of complex ER
casework end to end
+ building trusted relationships
quickly and constructively influencing and challenging stakeholders
+ using data and evidence to inform
decisions and communicate insights
+ maintaining accurate project and
case records
+ collaborating effectively and
adapting as priorities change
**Working arrangements**
This is 12-month fixed term contract. We are looking for someone to start as soon as possible. The contract will run for twelve months from the agreed start date.
This 12-month
fixed-term position has been created to provide additional specialist capacity
during a defined period of organisational change. It is an additional position
within the team and does not form part of the long-term team structure. The
contract is therefore expected to end after 12 months, when the current
programme of change and the associated need for additional capacity are due to
conclude. This is a hybrid role, where your work will be split between your home and one
day per week, on average, in our London office. This may vary from time to
time, so you will need to work in a flexible way to unlock your best work for
our cause.
This role requires occasional travel to other BHF locations for team
meeting and advisory meetings. **Belonging at BHF**
We are committed to fostering a
workplace where everyone feels valued and supported. Embracing different perspectives and
backgrounds strengthens our organisation and empowers us to make a real
difference together.
To hear from our people, check out Belonging at BHF. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. By funding research across six
decades, we’ve helped
keep millions of hearts beating and millions of families together. We’re investing in ground-breaking research
that will get us closer than ever to a world where everyone has a healthier
heart for longer. **Benefits and development**
At BHF, we
offer a comprehensive range of benefits designed to support our colleagues’
wellbeing and professional growth. To find out more about our benefits you can download the Benefits document at the bottom of this page or check out our Benefits and Development pages. Need more help balancing your work
and home life? Talk to us about what flexibility is available at the
application or interview stage. **Interview process** The interview process will consist
of two stages. First stage interviews will be held over MS Teams on w/c 16 Nov
2026. For those successful, there will be
second stage interviews in-person at our London Office (NW1 7AW) on
w/c 23 Nov 2026. **How to apply** It’s quick and easy to apply for a
role at the BHF. Just click on the apply button below. All you’ll need is an
up-to-date CV and answer three application questions.
Our recruitment processes are fair, accessible,
and inclusive. BHF use anonymous CV software as part of the
application journey. We support responsible use of AI to help shape your application. By applying
for a role at BHF, you confirm that your application is authentic and reflects
your own skills and experience, to ensure everyone is assessed fairly. Should you need any adjustments to the recruitment process, at either
application or interview, please contact
us.

internally this role will be known as People Relations Specialist – Change

# Job Description
Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage. Cresta’s unified AI platform combines conversational AI agents, real-time human agent augmentation, and comprehensive conversation intelligence to drive revenue and efficiency gains across every channel. The world’s leading companies, including United Airlines, Cox Communications, and Marriott, use Cresta to power world-class customer experiences every day.
Born from the Stanford AI Lab, Cresta has raised more than $270 million from the world’s leading investors, including a16z, Greylock, and Sequoia. Cresta’s leadership includes some of the leading minds in AI today. Our CEO, Ping Wu, founded and led Google's Contact Center AI and Vertex AI platforms before joining Cresta to build the future of AI-driven customer experiences.
Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day. Come build that future at Cresta.
**About the Role**
As our first EMEA **Forward Deployed Product Manager, AI Agent**, you will create, deploy and optimize AI Agents that transform our customers’ businesses and delight their customers. This highly cross-functional and customer-facing role blends product thinking, a nose for value, and project leadership with senior customer executives. At the end of the day, you own each AI Agent and the outcomes they drive for our customers, and you take that personally. You are a creative, pragmatic problem solver who thrives in fast-paced environments, rolls up your sleeves to build, and excels at turning ambiguity into execution.
In this role, you’ll partner with Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) who will support the build, integrations and optimization to make each AI Agent successful. You’ll also work closely with product and engineering, providing a tight feedback loop and custom tooling that will shape the future of our platform. As the first hire in EMEA, you’ll also play a key role in setting the standards for the role in the EMEA region and helping to grow the team as we scale.
**What You’ll Do**
* **Own AI Agent outcomes for our customers** — defining and delivering on the metrics that move the needle. This includes finding additional automation opportunities that can provide even more value! To do this, you’ll...
* **Own the deployment lifecycle** for AI Agents — from scoping and kickoff to launch and post-go-live optimization
* **Design, build, test and iterate on AI agents** in partnership with FDEs using Cresta’s internal tools and the latest technologies to deliver the highest customer ROI
* **Serve as the AI Agent SME for the EMEA Sales cycle,** partnering on demos, solutioning, and deal reviews to ensure technical feasibility, value articulation, and successful handoff to deployment.
* **Lead customer relationships** and act as the primary point of contact for AI Agent. Help customers move faster to ensure we can deliver quickly and effectively.
* **Facilitate workshops and design sessions** with customer stakeholders to align on agent use cases, workflows, and success criteria
* **Work closely with FDEs** to ensure smooth implementation, build new capabilities as needed and provide feedback and improvements to our broader platform
* **Improve our playbooks** for agent development and customer deployment
* **Build our forward deployed practice** for EMEA, setting the standards for future growth
**What We’re Looking For**
* 5+ years of experience in Technology Consulting, Implementations, Product, or Customer Success roles, ideally working closely with AI or LLM first products
* Hands-on work style – curiosity with a bias for action. You anticipate needs and bottlenecks and deliver with urgency and care.
* Experience leading complex deployments, owning customer relationships (including senior customer stakeholders), and working cross-functionally
* Strong technical understanding, systems thinking and exposure to building Agents (not necessarily conversational, personal projects count!)
* Comfortable working with ambiguity and learning quickly in a dynamic startup environment
* Passion for AI, automation, and shaping the future of customer experience
**Bonus Points**
* Background in product management, conversation design or forward deployed engineering roles
* Experience in a startup or high-growth SaaS environment
* Familiarity with customer support and contact center operations
**Perks & Benefits:**
We offer a comprehensive and people-first benefits package to support you at work and in life:
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with plans to fit you and your family
* Paid parental leave for all new parents welcoming a new child
* Remote work setup budget to help you create a productive home office
* Monthly wellness and communication stipend to keep you connected and balanced
* 20 days of vacation time
**Compensation at Cresta**
Cresta’s approach to compensation is simple: recognize impact, reward excellence, and invest in our people. We offer competitive, location-based pay that reflects the market and what each individual brings to the table.
Final offers are shaped by factors like experience, skills, education, and geography. In addition to base pay, total compensation includes equity and a comprehensive benefits package for you and your family.

* Build strong relationships with communities and partner organisations
* Work alongside Police Officers and other policing colleagues
* Help identify and respond to local concerns affecting the railway

Gas Safe Register is the official gas registration body for the United Kingdom, Isle of Man, Jersey and Guernsey. **Our Mission**
We’re on a mission to be a force for good in lending. Throughout our almost 30-year history, we’ve consistently been recognised as a great place to work; in 2026, Capital One was officially ranked 9th in the UK’s Best WorkplacesTM list. **Hear from our team** about what it’s like working at Capital One UK.
**About the Role**
As a Financial Services Disputes Lawyer, you will be responsible for leading the litigation strategy and managing a portfolio of consumer claims for Capital One. This portfolio mainly consists of residual PPI claims alongside a small number of other consumer claims. The role requires a highly strategic approach to handling litigation, including dealing with any threatened or issued group litigation and addressing any commercial disputes. Regular horizon scanning and preparing comprehensive reports for senior stakeholders on litigation trends will be essential parts of your remit to ensure the business is well prepared for emerging litigation risks. As well as engaging with any consultations which could impact the litigation landscape.
In addition to direct litigation management, you will play a critical advisory role for key first line operational functions. You will provide second-line support for section 75 Consumer Credit Act 1974 claims and disputed transactions, you will also be responsible for building and executing a merchant recovery strategy for s.75 claims. You will also provide second-line strategic support complaints, involving direct engagement with Claimant Firms and advising on complex and high-profile complaints.
**What you’ll do**
* **Lead Litigation & Strategy:** Manage a portfolio of consumer claims (primarily residual PPI and other ad-hoc claims), setting the overarching litigation strategies and proactive approaches to handle volumes and manage cases through to trial.
* **Group Litigation & Commercial Disputes:** Handle any threatened or issued group litigation effectively and efficiently, engaging and instructing external counsel on these claims where appropriate.
* **Commercial Contract Disputes:** Engaging with our contracts team where any commercial disputes arise, guiding them through any informal dispute resolution as well as dealing with any issued claims that may arise.
* **s.75 & Disputed Transactions:** Provide robust second-line support for the s.75 team and disputed transactions, including building and executing a merchant recovery strategy for s.75 claims.
* **Complaints Strategy:** Provide second-line support on the complaints strategy, including direct engagement with Claimant Firms and advising on complex, high-profile complaints.
* **Reporting & Horizon Scanning:** Conduct continuous horizon scanning to monitor key legal developments and litigation trends. Prepare reports and strategic updates for senior management.
* **External Engagement:** Manage external parties, including law firms and external counsel, to drive favourable outcomes.
* **Caseload Management:** Ensure compliance with court timetables, draft complex court documents, and conduct settlement negotiations.
* **Team Contribution:** Mentor junior team members and contribute to an engaging, inclusive, and high-performing team environment.
**The skills and experience you need**
* A qualified lawyer/solicitor with significant experience handling a caseload of consumer credit litigated claims and commercial disputes in private practice or an in-house legal team.
* Demonstrable experience dealing with s.75 claims, disputed transactions, and ideally building recovery strategies.
* Experience handling complex complaints and engaging effectively with Claims Management Companies (CMCs).
* Proven track record in setting and executing litigation strategies and experience with group litigation.
* Exceptional drafting skills for correspondence, strategic advice notes, and formal court documents.
* Strong legal research and horizon-scanning skills to preemptively identify risks.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities effectively and decisively.
* Demonstrates excellent judgment and problem solving capabilities.
* Proactive ownership of key tasks with excellent stakeholder management, reporting, and appropriate escalation.
* Results-focused and receptive to feedback, with a desire to own and drive continuous development.

This is a permanent position based in our **Nottingham office**. We embrace a hybrid approach to work. You'll spend three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday), with Monday and Friday being dedicated work-from-home days.

In addition to career development, our comprehensive benefits package is designed to grow with you, ensuring your wellbeing is prioritised at every stage of your career:

**Holidays:** Start with 25 days of annual leave, increasing with tenure. Need more? You have the option to buy 5 additional days.

**Job Title:** Financial Services Disputes Lawyer - Senior Associate
**Location:** Nottingham - Hybrid
**Working Pattern:** 3 days in-office (Tuesday-Thursday) and 2 days remote**.**
**Our Mission**
We’re on a mission to be a force for good in lending. Throughout our almost 30-year history, we’ve consistently been recognised as a great place to work; in 2026, Capital One was officially ranked 9th in the UK’s Best WorkplacesTM list. **Hear from our team** about what it’s like working at Capital One UK.
**About the Role**
As a Financial Services Disputes Lawyer, you will be responsible for leading the litigation strategy and managing a portfolio of consumer claims for Capital One. This portfolio mainly consists of residual PPI claims alongside a small number of other consumer claims. The role requires a highly strategic approach to handling litigation, including dealing with any threatened or issued group litigation and addressing any commercial disputes. Regular horizon scanning and preparing comprehensive reports for senior stakeholders on litigation trends will be essential parts of your remit to ensure the business is well prepared for emerging litigation risks. As well as engaging with any consultations which could impact the litigation landscape.
In addition to direct litigation management, you will play a critical advisory role for key first line operational functions. You will provide second-line support for section 75 Consumer Credit Act 1974 claims and disputed transactions, you will also be responsible for building and executing a merchant recovery strategy for s.75 claims. You will also provide second-line strategic support complaints, involving direct engagement with Claimant Firms and advising on complex and high-profile complaints.
**What you’ll do**
* **Lead Litigation & Strategy:** Manage a portfolio of consumer claims (primarily residual PPI and other ad-hoc claims), setting the overarching litigation strategies and proactive approaches to handle volumes and manage cases through to trial.
* **Group Litigation & Commercial Disputes:** Handle any threatened or issued group litigation effectively and efficiently, engaging and instructing external counsel on these claims where appropriate.
* **Commercial Contract Disputes:** Engaging with our contracts team where any commercial disputes arise, guiding them through any informal dispute resolution as well as dealing with any issued claims that may arise.
* **s.75 & Disputed Transactions:** Provide robust second-line support for the s.75 team and disputed transactions, including building and executing a merchant recovery strategy for s.75 claims.
* **Complaints Strategy:** Provide second-line support on the complaints strategy, including direct engagement with Claimant Firms and advising on complex, high-profile complaints.
* **Reporting & Horizon Scanning:** Conduct continuous horizon scanning to monitor key legal developments and litigation trends. Prepare reports and strategic updates for senior management.
* **External Engagement:** Manage external parties, including law firms and external counsel, to drive favourable outcomes.
* **Caseload Management:** Ensure compliance with court timetables, draft complex court documents, and conduct settlement negotiations.
* **Team Contribution:** Mentor junior team members and contribute to an engaging, inclusive, and high-performing team environment.
**The skills and experience you need**
* A qualified lawyer/solicitor with significant experience handling a caseload of consumer credit litigated claims and commercial disputes in private practice or an in-house legal team.
* Demonstrable experience dealing with s.75 claims, disputed transactions, and ideally building recovery strategies.
* Experience handling complex complaints and engaging effectively with Claims Management Companies (CMCs).
* Proven track record in setting and executing litigation strategies and experience with group litigation.
* Exceptional drafting skills for correspondence, strategic advice notes, and formal court documents.
* Strong legal research and horizon-scanning skills to preemptively identify risks.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities effectively and decisively.
* Demonstrates excellent judgment and problem solving capabilities.
* Proactive ownership of key tasks with excellent stakeholder management, reporting, and appropriate escalation.
* Results-focused and receptive to feedback, with a desire to own and drive continuous development.
**Where and how you'll work**
This is a permanent position based in our **Nottingham office**. We embrace a hybrid approach to work. You'll spend three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday), with Monday and Friday being dedicated work-from-home days.
Our offices are designed to inspire and support you. At our Nottingham head office, you'll find an on-site gym, restaurant and dedicated Learning Loft. Our London office boasts a rooftop running track and coffee bar.
**What’s in it for you**
We invest in the growth of our people alongside our business. You will have extensive opportunities to learn and develop your career, including access to up to £5,000 in funding for external qualifications.
In addition to career development, our comprehensive benefits package is designed to grow with you, ensuring your wellbeing is prioritised at every stage of your career:
**Wealth & Future:** Competitive pension and performance-based bonus schemes
**Holidays:** Start with 25 days of annual leave, increasing with tenure. Need more? You have the option to buy 5 additional days.
**Health:** Access premium care through our private medical insurance.
**Family Support:** We champion your milestones with enhanced parental leave.
A full list of our benefits is available **here**.

We pride ourselves on hiring the best people, not the same people. Building diverse and inclusive teams is the right thing to do and the smart thing to do. We want to work with top talent: whoever you are, whatever you look like, wherever you come from. We know it’s about what you do, not just what you say. That’s why we make our recruitment process fair and accessible.
We value diversity, inclusion and belonging at our core. We empower our associates to do great work by creating an inclusive culture—one that values diverse perspectives, fosters collaboration and encourages innovative ideas—and a place where associates of all backgrounds can thrive by bringing their most authentic selves to work. We call this our Culture of Belonging, and it rests at the heart of our business.
Our associate-led Business Resource Groups were created to help support our diverse population and include over 10 groups across our offices.
