# Head of Engineering & Data (UK)
## Are you a tech leader who gets the best from systems, data and partners? Help us choose and optimise the right solutions to power our next stage of growth as a fast-paced, scaling business. Apply now!
***Head of Engineering & Data - UK***
***Salary: c£100K+ dependent on experience***
***Location: Glasgow, UK (hybrid – home working plus 3 days per week in our Glasgow hub)***
Are you a technology leader who knows how to get the best out of systems, data and development partners? Someone who understands that great technology isn't always about building something new, but about choosing the right solutions, connecting them effectively and making them work brilliantly? If you thrive in a fast-paced, scaling environment and want to shape how technology supports our next stage of growth, we'd love to hear from you.
This is a fantastic opportunity to play a key role in shaping how technology and data support the future of Macs Adventure. We're a tech-enabled travel company, not a software house. We buy and integrate most of our technology, working with external development partners who build, maintain and support our systems. You'll be responsible for ensuring our technology works together, is secure and reliable, and can scale with our ambitions.
Reporting to our Technology & Digital Director, you'll own our technical architecture and engineering standards, grow a small team of specialists and work hand in hand with trusted development partners to turn our technology strategy into practical solutions that support our journey to become the world's leading active travel company.
**About Macs Adventure**
We’re a scaling adventure tour operator on a mission to be the leading global brand in self-guided, active travel.
Welcoming over 40,000 customers on walking and cycling trips to destinations around the world, we employ over 150 people across the UK, US and Germany who share our purpose to **create #macsmoments by** **leading, advocating & enabling self-guided, active travel as a positive force for people and planet.**
**Our Culture**
We’re an ambitious, forward-thinking business with a bold vision for the future, and our culture reflects these ambitions. We’re an action-oriented, fast-paced organisation and we like to have fun along the way. We’re looking for people who can grow with Macs and grow with us on our journey to become the world’s leading active travel company. It’s not the easy route and we’re looking for people who enjoy challenges, love learning, want to make an impact and align with our core values:
· **Love the journey:** A Macs trip is all about the journey, not the destination. We are all believers in Macs’ unique brand of self-guided, active travel and shout about it. As more travellers convert to the Macs Way, we accept our business will grow and change. We welcome new connections and embrace new opportunities. Carpe diem!
· **Take a different path**: We’re not different for different’s sake; but we won’t succeed if we’re just the same as everyone else. We devise creative solutions to problems, find new ways of doing things, and trust colleagues who are doing so too. We are brave and feel empowered to take the initiative. We ask ourselves: is what I’m doing authentically Macs?
· **Tread thoughtfully:** We are considerate, empathetic and try to put ourselves in our customers’, suppliers’ and each other’s shoes. We support local and find ways of having less negative impact on the planet. We find ways of having positive impact on people and communities. We are fair, and we do the right thing.
· **Go the extra mile:** We know that creating a perfect #MacsMoment involves going that bit further. We imagine the best feedback we can get and set out to earn it. We take ownership and accountability – it’s yours, not someone else’s, problem. We step up and help our teammates when they need us.
**What you’ll do;**
We work with trusted development partners who build, maintain and support our applications, including the cloud infrastructure behind them. Alongside them, we have a deliberately small internal team of engineering and data specialists who bring technical expertise and a deep understanding of Macs. Together, they work as one team to make sure our technology delivers what the business needs.
Our internal specialists work within cross-functional squads alongside colleagues from Product, UX and Marketing. The business defines the problem, and the squad works together to find the best solution. As Head of Engineering & Data, you'll provide the technical leadership that brings this together, setting clear standards and making architecture decisions whilst supporting your team's development through coaching and influence, rather than directing their day-to-day work.
Here's where you'll make an impact:
* **Strengthen our core technology platforms:** improving the stability and reliability of our key systems, whilst gradually reducing our reliance on any single critical supplier through planned, manageable changes rather than a disruptive, large-scale re-platforming.
* **Be our architect-of-record:** own the system map, integration standards and decision log, so every choice is coherent and stands up to investor scrutiny.
* **Lead technology selection and integration:** guiding the technical evaluation of new systems and working with our squads and development partners to ensure everything connects effectively and works together as one product.
* **Own our data platform:** ensuring we have a lean, modern data platform that gives the business one trusted source of information, whilst supporting our marketing technology and customer-facing products.
* **Drive the use of AI across Macs:** identifying and delivering opportunities to use AI across our people, processes and products. From reducing manual work and costs to enabling teams to build their own AI agents and integrating AI into our products, you'll ensure every initiative has clear ownership and measurable targets.
* **Set our engineering standards:** establishing clear requirements, automated testing and consistent ways of working that help our internal squads and external partners deliver quality solutions predictably.
* **Keep our technology secure, compliant and resilient:** ensuring we have the right controls in place to protect our systems and data, whilst overseeing our cloud infrastructure and technology suppliers, including their costs.
* **Manage our technology partners and suppliers:** building strong relationships with our external partners and holding them accountable for the quality and reliability of the services they provide.
* **Lead and develop our internal team:** growing a small, experienced team of engineering and data specialists, supporting their career development through coaching and technical guidance whilst enabling them to contribute effectively within their cross-functional squads.
**What you’ll bring;**
* Experience as a senior engineering leader (Head of Engineering, VP Engineering or similar), comfortable being the most senior technologist in the business.
* A compose-not-build instinct: strong judgement in choosing and integrating third-party platforms, building only where it truly sets us apart.
* A track record with external development partners, including de-risking or replacing a critical system without breaking the business.
* Technical depth – hands-on enough to challenge partners and get into the detail of cloud, integration and data architecture, without needing to write the code yourself.
* Personal ownership of a data platform and BI estate as well as engineering – for us, this is one job, not two.
* The drive to push AI forward across people, processes and product – with measurable results.
* Solid security, compliance and resilience fundamentals.
* A habit of writing things down, and the standing to hold architecture decisions and explain them to leaders, partners and investors alike.
* A coaching style: you build small, senior teams and help people grow, rather than building empires.
**Not essential, it would be a bonus if you;**
* Worked in a consumer digital, e-commerce or travel scale-up.
* Delivered AI with measurable impact – for example AI agents, agent-ready APIs or AI built into a customer-facing product.
* Built or worked with a data platform that brings structured data (bookings, finance, operations) together with unstructured text (documents, reviews, emails), so people and AI agents can perform natural-language queries and get answers drawn from both.
* ERP, CRS or CRM platform evaluation.
* AWS/Azure cloud consolidation.
* Supported an investor technical due diligence process.
* A genuine love of the outdoors, walking or cycling, and a passion for active travel
The knowledge and skills we’ve listed represent “the perfect candidate”. No one’s perfect and we know the ‘confidence gap’ can stop brilliant people applying. If you love the sound of this opportunity please apply, we’d love to hear from you.
**You could belong here;**
To deliver adventures for more than 40,000 customers we need to build a company that’s reflective of their diversity. We’re building an inclusive workplace that promotes and values difference, where everyone, from any background, can do their best work and be proud to belong.
**What we’ll offer**
As well as your salary;
* **ANNUAL LEAVE:** We want you to be able to take holidays that matter to you, so 8 public holidays are included in your annual leave allowance of 33 days, which increases to 35 days after 5 years’ service.
* **BIRTHDAY BOOSTER:** An extra day off on your birthday!
* **PENSION:** We offer a contributory pension scheme.
* **DISCOUNTS:** Enjoy generous discounts on Macs Adventure trips — you'll get to experience the same self-guided adventures we create for our customers, at a price that makes it easy to say yes. It's a perk built around what we love doing most: getting outside and exploring!
* **TRAVEL INSURANCE:** We provide you and your spouse/partner/children with annual worldwide travel insurance.
* **FLEXIBLE WORKING:** A flexible work culture - you’ll be able to work from home as well as coming into our hub office in Glasgow 3 days per week to collaborate with colleagues.
* **GETTING TOGETHER:** Regular team, management and leadership meetings and retreats.
* **CULTURE:** An innovative, fast growth, international and solution focused culture, where we work hard to embed our values across the business.
* **L&D:** We support your self-guided learning journey to make the most of your strengths.
* **WELLBEING**. We'll support you in looking after your health and wellbeing so you can do your best work.
* **TRAVEL:** Occasional international travel may be required.
* **IMPACT:** The opportunity to make a difference in people’s lives and the planet.

# Job purpose
The Clinical Administrator provides accurate, compassionate and well-organised administrative support within the primary care team. The postholder will coordinate care-home activity, referrals, clinical forms and follow-up work, helping patients, carers, clinicians and external services receive the right information at the right time.

• Act as a central administrative contact for the care homes supported by the practice, communicating professionally with care-home staff, residents’ representatives, patients and carers.
• Prepare accurate patient lists and relevant administrative information for GP care-home ward rounds, checking that known requests and outstanding actions are clearly identified.
• Following each ward round, enter or upload agreed information and actions into EMIS in line with practice protocols, ensuring the clinical record accurately reflects the clinician’s instructions.
• Track actions arising from ward rounds, chase responses and coordinate follow-up appointments, tests, prescriptions or referrals as directed.
• Liaise with care homes between ward rounds to obtain information, progress requests and route clinical questions or concerns to the relevant GP.
• Coordinate long-term condition reviews for care-home residents, including identifying patients due for review and arranging the required appointments or information.
• Organise pharmacist ward rounds and seasonal influenza vaccination rounds, including lists, scheduling, communications and follow-up administration.
• Attend occasional care-home meetings and visit care homes when operationally required.
## 2. Referrals, forms and clinical correspondence
• Complete ADHD referral forms under agreed pathways and protocols, using information provided by the patient, parent or carer.
• Contact patients, parents, carers or other appropriate representatives to gather the information required for other referral forms and questionnaires, using sensitive and clear communication.
• Draft referral forms for review and approval by the relevant GP or authorised clinician; check that approved referrals are submitted correctly and recorded.
• Complete maternity returns and other routine clinical forms under agreed protocols.
• Prepare other referral forms, clinical questionnaires, reports and supporting letters, seeking clinician input and approval where required.
• Monitor referrals and forms through to completion, chasing missing information or external responses and keeping patients or carers appropriately informed.
## 3. Patient and carer communication
• Communicate confidently by telephone and in writing, adapting the approach for people who may be anxious, vulnerable, unwell or have additional communication needs.
• Listen with empathy, gather information accurately and explain administrative processes, likely next steps and expected timescales without offering clinical advice.
• Maintain appropriate consent, confidentiality and identity checks when communicating with patients, partners, family members and carers.
• Recognise when information indicates a possible clinical, safeguarding or welfare concern and escalate it promptly through the correct practice route.
## 4. Workflow, records and follow-up
• Prepare and process clinical administrative work under agreed practice protocols and standard operating procedures.
• Maintain clear task lists or trackers, prioritise work, monitor deadlines and follow outstanding actions through to completion.
• Code agreed information accurately into EMIS within the postholder’s training, competence and authorised role boundaries.
• Book or coordinate follow-up appointments and communicate arrangements to patients, carers, care homes and relevant team members.
• Check work for accuracy, completeness and correct patient details before submission, filing or onward transfer.
• Contribute to service improvement by identifying recurring delays, gaps or risks and suggesting practical changes to the Primary Care Team Lead.
## 5. Team working and governance
• Work closely with the Primary Care Team Lead, GPs, pharmacists, nurses, administrative colleagues, care-home staff and external providers.
• Manage day-to-day workload independently while seeking support when priorities conflict or work falls outside agreed protocols.
• Follow practice policies for confidentiality, information governance, data protection, safeguarding, health and safety, equality and infection prevention.
• Undertake required training, supervision and appraisal, and maintain competence in relevant systems and processes.
• Provide reasonable cross-cover within the primary care team and work flexibly across Manor View Practice sites when required.
# Key working relationships
Primary Care Team Lead; GP partners and salaried GPs; pharmacists and pharmacy technicians; nursing and wider clinical teams; practice administrative teams; care-home managers and staff; patients, carers and authorised representatives; community, secondary-care and referral services.

**About the team:**
Our Borrowing (lending) business is growing rapidly across both existing products and with the planned launch of new initiatives. As our lending portfolio grows, our second line of defence Credit Model Validation team is growing with it - and we’re looking for a Credit Model Validation Manager to join us!
Our Credit Model Validation team provides independent oversight and challenge to our model development teams in the first line of defence. We help Monzo grow safely and make sure the models we use are fit for purpose, appropriately governed and deliver good outcomes for our customers. You’ll join our validation squad and provide expert independent validation and oversight across a broad suite of credit models.
This is a generalist role rather than one focused on a particular model type. You’ll work across models used for impairment, capital, stress testing, forecasting and credit decisioning, including IFRS 9 PD, LGD, EAD and economic response models; decision science scorecards and origination PD models; and Net Present Value (NPV) / unit economics models.
Strong data and analytical skills are a must, as is broad expertise in credit risk modelling and model risk management. You’ll have hands-on experience in model validation and/or development within financial services, and be comfortable getting into the data and code to form an independent view across different model types.
**Your day-to-day**
* Leading hands-on independent validation across Monzo’s credit model portfolio - covering models used for IFRS 9 impairment, capital and stress testing, forecasting, credit decisioning and unit economics - and making sure they are fit for purpose, appropriately governed and performing as expected
* Reviewing and challenging key model-led credit risk assessments, including impairment adequacy, ICAAP and stress testing, using independent analysis to assess assumptions, limitations and impacts
* Developing a deep understanding of Monzo’s credit models and how they are used, and using this to provide impactful input and challenge to model developers and users
* Contributing to making model validation more consistent, scalable and technology-enabled - building reusable analytical tools and tests, experimenting with AI-assisted approaches and helping the team embed them safely
* Reviewing ongoing model performance monitoring to ensure our lending models perform within our risk thresholds, and providing support to our first line of defence teams when action is required
* Performing statistical analyses, model replication and challenger work where appropriate to test assumptions, assess performance and strengthen validation conclusions
* Improving and helping to embed our Model Risk Framework, including our policies, standards, model inventory, governance and validation approach. This means making sure we follow up-to-date regulatory expectations and that our processes remain proportionate and relevant as modelling techniques evolve
* Writing clear and impactful model validation reports, and presenting the findings and actions in relevant committees
* Partnering with colleagues in first line of defence credit strategy, modelling and finance teams - and with wider risk teams across Monzo - to support effective model governance and consistent validation standards across the organisation
### **You should apply if you:**
* Have a strong background and practical experience in credit model development and/or validation across a range of model types. You’ll have meaningful experience with IFRS 9 impairment, Internal Ratings Based (IRB) or other capital models, alongside broader exposure to several areas such as stress testing, economic response, forecasting, decision science scorecards or NPV / unit economics modelling
* Understand model risk management in practice, including independent validation, model governance, ongoing monitoring, model change and issue management, and how regulatory expectations apply across the model lifecycle
* Are impact-driven and want to improve how validation is done, not only complete individual reviews. You can turn repeatable work into practical methods, tools or guidance that improve quality and consistency across the team.
* Are curious about AI and automation, and can assess where they add value, the risks they introduce, and the controls and human oversight needed. Experience with AI-assisted analytical or coding tools is useful, but not essential
* Are data driven, with strong analytical skills and deep knowledge of statistical techniques for credit and model risk. Strong SQL and Python skills are essential. You can produce clear, reusable and tested code, using collaborative practices such as version control, peer review and documentation. Experience with Tableau, Looker or similar is a plus.
* Can assess models in the context of how they are used - including accounting, capital, credit strategy, risk appetite and customer outcomes - and can distinguish technical model performance from the wider risks of relying on the model
* Have strong written and verbal communication skills, and are able to articulate problems and solutions using clear and simple language. This is particularly important for breaking down complex issues and priorities to non-experts
* Have a track record of building and maintaining trusting relationships with stakeholders at all levels, and can provide effective and respectful challenge
**Our technology stack**
We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies (note we do not expect applicants to have prior experience of all them):
* Google Cloud Platform for all of our analytics infrastructure
* dbt and BigQuery SQL for our data modelling and warehousing
* Python for data science and machine learning
* Go to write our application code
* AWS for most of our backend infrastructure

Our interview process usually involves up to four main stages via Google Meet:
* An initial call with our recruiter
* A call with our Senior Model Validation Manager, the hiring manager for the role

## About the job
**Join NETbuilder at a pivotal stage of growth and help scale a differentiated managed security services business.**
## About NETbuilder
NETbuilder is a rapidly growing, disruptive security services provider with a global footprint and a clear ambition: to redefine how organizations consume managed security services in an AI-driven threat landscape.
We are a leader in AI Managed Security Services and Security Engineering, combining innovative, differentiated offerings with deep engineering expertise and measurable customer outcomes. As a strategic partner of CrowdStrike and Splunk, we help customers maximize the value of their security platforms, strengthen resilience against modern threats, and prepare for emerging malicious AI activity.
Our mission is to secure our customers against modern threats, future adversaries, and emerging malicious AI activity through high-quality services tailored to their platforms and environments.
Every investment a customer makes with NETbuilder should improve security posture and increase operational efficiency. We achieve this by applying the right expertise, services, and tools at every critical stage.
## **About the Team**
NETbuilder’s Managed Security Services practice specializes in running and improving security operations for mid-market and enterprise customers using the platforms in which they have already invested.
This is an early-stage opportunity with proven traction. NETbuilder has already onboarded its first fourteen managed security services customers and is now building the sales engine, partner motion, and delivery capacity required to expand that base to hundreds of customers.
We have distinct offerings for our two core markets. Enterprise customers receive tailored, engineering-led services for complex security environments, including co-managed and fully managed operations. Mid-market customers receive standardized, outcome-focused services designed for rapid onboarding, predictable value, and scalable protection.
Our expertise spans CrowdStrike Next-Gen SIEM, Splunk, and Cisco Security. We deliver holistic security services across detection engineering, telemetry and data-source health, threat intelligence, and 24/7/365 SOC monitoring and incident response.
We offer two primary engagement models:
* **Augmenting existing security operations teams.** We work alongside customers’ internal security teams, restoring valuable time and capacity so they can focus on critical security priorities, actions, and initiatives.
* **Running day-to-day security operations.** We take ownership and accountability for security operations on our customers’ behalf, operating 24/7/365. We improve security posture and data maturity while providing a clear path for service transition when the customer is ready.
We position ourselves as a managed service partner, not simply a managed service vendor: communication-first, engineering-led, and accountable for outcomes.
The practice is growing rapidly, and this role will be central to how we turn early customer success into a repeatable global growth business.
## **About the Role**
Are you highly motivated and relentlessly focused on achieving the best outcomes for your customers?
Do you have an inquisitive mindset and a genuine desire to learn in an ever-evolving security landscape?
Are you successful yet humble, with a partner-first, customer-centric approach to creating shared success?
If this sounds like you, read on...
This is a critical, high-impact hire for NETbuilder as we accelerate growth across the United Kingdom. You will build your business by landing new logos, co-selling with our strategic platform and channel partners, and growing existing accounts across our enterprise and mid-market propositions.
You will own opportunities from the first conversation through the initial contract and beyond. You will lead discovery with security leaders, shape engagements alongside our solutions and service delivery teams, and close multi-year recurring-revenue agreements.
This is an individual-contributor sales leadership role reporting directly to the VP of Sales, EMEA. You will work closely with internal stakeholders, including our CISO and Global Head of Managed Services.
The territory and sales playbook are still being built. You will have the opportunity to shape both, influence how we take our differentiated offerings to market, and work directly with the managed services leadership and delivery organization behind what you sell.
## **What You’ll Do**
* **Hunt for new business.** Build and manage pipeline through outbound prospecting into security and IT leadership teams at mid-market and enterprise organizations.
* **Help turn early traction into scale.** Build on our base of existing managed security services customers by developing repeatable sales motions that can support growth to hundreds.
* **Activate the partner ecosystem.** Develop strong relationships with CrowdStrike and Splunk field sellers, as well as reseller and distribution partners. Source referred and co-sold opportunities and keep NETbuilder top of mind within their accounts.
* **Run the full sales cycle.** Lead discovery, qualify opportunities against our engagement models, coordinate scoping with our solutions and delivery teams, develop proposals and statements of work with sales leadership, and negotiate through close.
* **Sell to two distinct markets.** Position NETbuilder’s enterprise and mid-market offerings clearly, adapting the value proposition, commercial approach, and sales motion to each customer’s needs.
* **Grow existing accounts.** Own managed security services sales across an agreed portfolio of existing services customers, identifying opportunities to protect, renew, and expand each relationship.
* **Sell consultatively.** Translate SOC operations, detection engineering, SIEM, and AI security concepts into meaningful business outcomes for CISOs, Security Directors, and SOC Managers. You will be comfortable contributing to technical conversations alongside our engineers.
* **Keep the system honest.** Maintain accurate pipeline, forecast, and activity data in our CRM, contributing to a forecast the business can confidently plan around.
* **Show up in the market.** Represent NETbuilder at industry events, partner events, and customer meetings, with travel as required.
## **What You’ll Bring**
* **3-5+ years of quota-carrying B2B sales experience,** including at least two years selling Managed Security Services such as MDR, MSSP, managed SIEM, SOC-as-a-Service, or co-managed security operations.
* **A strong working knowledge of the cybersecurity market.** You understand what a SOC does, how SIEM and EDR/XDR fit together, and why organizations invest in managed detection and response. You can speak credibly with the people responsible for running security programs.
* **A track record of closing recurring-revenue service engagements** involving MRR or ARR, rather than solely professional services, product, or license transactions. You have experience navigating multi-stakeholder deals involving security, IT, procurement, and legal teams.
* **Experience working within partner ecosystems,** including channel partners, distributors, or technology alliance programs. You have the instincts and experience to build pipeline through partners rather than around them.
* **Strong discovery and consultative selling skills.** You diagnose before you prescribe and scope engagements that customers can grow with rather than quickly churn out of.
* **Disciplined pipeline management and CRM hygiene.** You maintain accurate records and forecast what you genuinely expect to close.
* **Highly preferred based in London,** with the ability to travel for customer, partner, and industry engagements.
* **A naturally curious and inquisitive mindset,** with a commitment to continually expanding your knowledge in an ever-evolving security landscape.
## **Nice to Have**
* **Direct experience within the CrowdStrike or Splunk ecosystems,** whether selling the platforms themselves, selling services built around them, or co-selling alongside their field teams. Experience with Cisco Security is also valuable.
* **An existing network of security buyers,** including CISOs, Security Directors, and SOC leaders, or channel relationships you can activate.
* **Familiarity with how managed security engagements are scoped and contracted,** including statements of work, service tiers, onboarding timelines, and renewal cycles.
* **Experience working in a high-growth services business** where sellers help shape the playbook, proposition, and routes to market rather than simply execute an established model.
## **What Success Looks Like**
In your first year, you will have:
* **Built a self-sustaining pipeline** across direct, vendor and channel-partner routes to market.
* **Closed new managed security services customers** and created meaningful multi-year recurring revenue.
* **Advanced our scale-up journey** from an initial base of 14 customers toward a business capable of supporting hundreds.
* **Protected and expanded** your renewal portfolio.
* **Become a seller that partners actively bring into their customer accounts,** particularly across the CrowdStrike and Splunk ecosystems.
* **Developed a strong understanding of our service catalog** and the ability to position our enterprise and mid-market offerings confidently.
* **Made a meaningful contribution** to improving the sales playbook, propositions, and go-to-market approach.
**You will leave the sales playbook better than you found it.**

# AIT Systems Integration Engineer
## Location
Reading, UK
## Employment Type
Full time
## Location Type
Hybrid
## Department
SatelliteAIT
## Deadline to Apply
November 29, 2026 at 4:00 PM PST
OverviewApplication
## **Company**
NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.
Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.
Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.
Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.
## Role
The AIT Systems Integration Engineer owns functional and system-level testing of our spacecraft and the verification tracking for each satellite campaign. Working within the Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) team, you will take the satellite from integrated subsystems to a flight-ready, fully verified vehicle.
You will bridge systems engineering, subsystem teams and the AIT Engineering Functions. You will turn requirements into test procedures, run and lead test campaigns, and make sure every requirement is closed out with traceable evidence before launch.
The role suits someone who knows SmallSat development approaches, is hands-on with Hardware and Ground Support Equipment (GSE), and understands how satellite subsystems behave together.
## Responsibilities
### Functional and system testing
* Own the functional and system test programme for the spacecraft, from unit-level acceptance, integration, thought to whole System End-to-End Testing.
* Write, review and run test specifications and procedures, including basic functional testing, FDIR, end-to-end tests and mission/day-in-the-life simulations.
* Lead test readiness reviews and test review boards, and sign off test reports.
* Run tests before, during and after environmental campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMC) to confirm spacecraft health.
* Diagnose anomalies, raise and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and drive root-cause investigations with subsystem engineers.
* Develop and maintain automated test scripts and telemetry/telecommand (TM/TC) databases used for testing.
### Verification tracking
* Own the verification matrix (VCRM) for the satellite campaign, mapping each requirement to its method: test, analysis, inspection or review of design.
* Plan the verification approach with Systems Engineering and keep it current through the campaign.
* Collect and link verification evidence, and report close-out status against milestones.
* Prepare verification data packages for key reviews (e.g. CDR, TRR, QR, PSR/FAR) and customer acceptance.
### GSE and test infrastructure
* Specify, integrate and validate Electrical GSE, including power supplies, battery simulators, RF test sets, umbilicals and break-out boxes.
* Maintain the spacecraft checkout software and ground segment interfaces used on the AIT floor.
* Make sure GSE is calibrated, configuration-controlled and safe for use with flight hardware.
### Integration and campaign support
* Support subsystem and payload integration, including electrical interface checks, harness verification and safe-to-mate procedures.
* Plan and schedule system test activities within the wider AIT campaign.
* Support launch campaign activities, including transport, launch site checkout and launch vehicle interface testing.
* Work to cleanroom, ESD and flight hardware handling standards, and contribute to lessons learned for future missions.
## Requirements
* Degree in Aerospace, Electronic, Electrical or Systems Engineering, Physics, or equivalent experience.
* Typically 3+ years in spacecraft AIT, systems integration or test engineering.
* Hands-on experience with functional and system-level testing of satellites or space subsystems.
* Familiarity with SmallSat development approaches: agile, rapid iteration, protoflight models, and pragmatic use of COTS components.
* Working knowledge of satellite subsystems: EPS, OBC/C&DH, ADCS, communications (TT&C and payload RF), propulsion, thermal, structures and payloads.
* Experience using and setting up GSE, including EGSE, checkout systems and RF test equipment.
* Experience with requirements verification and maintaining a verification matrix through to close-out.
* Comfortable with lab equipment: oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, spectrum analysers, logic analysers.
* Familiarity with common spacecraft interfaces and protocols (e.g. CAN, I2C, SPI, RS-422, SpaceWire, CCSDS).
* Clear technical writing for procedures, test reports and NCRs.
## Desirables
* End-to-end involvement in at least one satellite mission that reached launch.
* Test automation and scripting in Python or similar, and experience with spacecraft control or checkout software (e.g. OpenC3/COSMOS, Yamcs, SCOS-2000).
* Experience planning or supporting environmental test campaigns (vibration, TVAC, EMC).
* Knowledge of ECSS standards (e.g. ECSS-E-ST-10-02 Verification, ECSS-E-ST-10-03 Testing) or NASA equivalents.
* Requirements management tools (e.g. DOORS, Jama, Polarion, Valispace).
* Launch campaign experience at a launch site.
* Cleanroom and ESD-certified flight hardware handling.
* Eligibility for UK security clearance, or the ability to obtain it, if required by the programme.
## Personal attributes
* Takes ownership: drives tests and verification to close-out without waiting to be asked.
* Methodical and detail-focused, with a strong sense of safety and quality around flight hardware.
* Calm, structured problem-solver when anomalies appear under schedule pressure.
* Communicates clearly across disciplines, from subsystem engineers to programme managers and customers.
* Comfortable in a fast-paced SmallSat environment, balancing rigour with pace.
* Willing to work flexibly during test and launch campaigns, including occasional travel.
## **Why NewOrbit Space?**
* **Pioneering space technology** - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.
* **Ownership and impact** - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.
* **Equity and competitive salary** - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.
* **Comprehensive benefits** - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.
* **Hybrid working** - One dedicated remote day per week.
* **Visa sponsorship and relocation support** - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.

We’re deploying large-scale NVIDIA GPU clusters, including GB200 and GB300 rack-scale systems, into live data centres on tight customer commit dates. We need one architect per deployment who takes the high-level design and turns it into something that can actually be built, then stays with it until the customer signs off.
This is a role for someone who would rather find the problem on paper than on the data hall floor. It suits someone who will push back on an inherited design or a customer requirement that won’t perform, and who carries authority through owning the design rather than managing people.
**WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING**

* Take each cluster from CTO handover to customer acceptance as its single design authority, so nothing is ordered or installed against a design you haven’t validated
* Turn high-level designs and initial BOMs into build-ready low-level designs, hall layouts, rack elevations, P2P maps and cable schedules that site teams can build from without having to call you
* Design the InfiniBand and Ethernet fabric, power, direct liquid cooling and containment to fit the real constraints of each data centre
* Validate every BOM before it goes to procurement, and make part substitution calls knowing exactly what breaks when a line changes
* Hold OEMs and integrators (NVIDIA, Dell, Lenovo, Supermicro and others) to their technical commitments, from FAT witness through to on-site issue resolution

* Deep, practical knowledge of NVIDIA platforms (GB200/GB300 rack-scale and HGX H200/B200) and what each one demands of a facility
* Cluster-scale InfiniBand and Ethernet fabric design: topology, rail optimisation, oversubscription, and cable and optic selection
* Physical infrastructure design across power and redundancy, direct liquid cooling and CDUs, containment and achievable cable lengths
* You know part numbers, what’s optional and what isn’t, and you can hold an OEM to account when their commitments slip
*Nice to Have:*
* Factory integration and FAT experience, including holding a dispatch gate
* Storage design for AI workloads (WEKA, VAST, DDN, Ceph or similar)
* Deployments across multiple geographies and data centre operators, including sites requiring fit-out

As our R&D Development engineer, you'll be the technical architect behind innovative roofing solutions that solve real-world construction challenges. Your expertise in CAD technology will drive product innovation, ensuring every design not only meets the highest industry standards but also advances Nicholson's reputation as the go-to specialist for complex roofing system solutions. You'll be instrumental in our continued growth, working closely with Tier 1 contractors and architects to deliver bespoke engineering solutions that make the impossible, possible.

This role requires a strong engineering foundation, practical problem-solving ability, and the confidence to take responsibility for progressing R&D work packages through relevant stages of our product development process. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with the R&D Manager and wider business, contributing to design, prototyping, testing and documentation activities that support robust, evidence-led product development.
This is a practical engineering role suited to someone who enjoys turning partially defined problems into well-considered, testable solutions, and who is comfortable working across CAD, workshop, and testing environments.
Key Goals for first 6 months:
* 80% of Scorecard achieved
* Able to confidently handle an R&D project all the way from Ideation to manufacture

Other Benefits:
5 sick days on full pay Free lunches
Buy or sell holiday scheme
Birthday voucher Free On-Site Parking NEST Pension scheme Health insurance scheme, including discounted gym membership and appointment paybacks

Reports to: R&D Manager
Main Duties & Responsibilities
Concept Development & Feasibility
* Contribute engineering insight to early-stage idea generation and feasibility discussions
* Review proposed concepts and solutions from a range of sources, including internal idea submissions
* Evaluate solution options using technical, practical and performance-based considerations
* Translate approved concepts into clear development objectives and draft briefs for further review
* Ensure sufficient information is available to support informed project decisions
Detailed Specification:
* Design the concept on CAD - both 2D and 3D
* Develop the performance criteria
* Conduct desktop testing in a virtual environment, e.g. stress analysis
* Create a technical specification
* Create the Specification Summary Report
Prototype Development:
* Extract part files from CAD models and raise procurement requests for prototype components
* Fabricate or modify parts as required to support prototyping activities
* Assemble physical prototypes to assess functionality, buildability and performance
* Coordinate external testing activities where required to support compliance or validation
* Finalise prototype builds and ensure all relevant information is documented
* Prepare Prototype Summary Reports and share outcomes with stakeholders
Testing & Validation:
* Develop and execute testing methodologies in line with agreed R&D and compliance requirements
* Prepare test rigs and equipment for internal testing activities
* Conduct internal testing for functionality, structural performance and weathering integrity
* Collect test data from sensors, measurements and observations
* Record, analyse and present test data in clear and meaningful formats
* Draft test reports in line with agreed internal standards
Cross-functional Collaboration:
* Work closely with design, marketing, and sales teams to bring products through the R&D process, to market
* Facilitate communication and collaboration between different departments to ensure product success
* Coordinate with quality assurance team to ensure product quality and reliability
There may be additional duties to the above.
KPIs
* Throughput of projects in accordance with the weekly department plan - target zero discrepancy
What We're Looking For
Skills, Experience, Qualifications required
* Previous experience (6 months or more) in R&D for a construction product, in a large organisation
* Good understanding of the built environment and building envelope and construction principles
* Understands and is qualified in engineering, such as mechanical engineering degree.
* Strong practical problem-solving skills, with the ability to progress defined work packages independently
* Well organised, with the ability to manage tasks across multiple development activities
* Practical, hands on candidate, with exposure to metalwork and engineering e.g. welding, drilling, folding, test rigs etc.
* Fluent in Autocad 2D and 3D design (ideally Inventor)
* Demonstrable experience of ability to provide tangible solutions
* Strong Project management skills, able to take projects through all stages of the R&D process
* A full UK work authorisation without the need for current or future sponsorship
* Alignment with, and commitment to the Nicholson company values
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* The candidate should have a range of GCSE / A Level results which show passes in English and Mathematics
Personal Attributes
You are someone aligned to the Nicholson Values of Humility, Agility, Focus, Enthusiasm, and Integrity.
You are someone who thrives on getting things done properly and seeing projects through to completion. Your natural approach is methodical and systematic - you like to follow processes, take detailed notes, and ensure everything meets required standards. You genuinely care about accuracy and take pride in producing high-quality technical work. You're comfortable focusing on your own tasks without needing constant social interaction, preferring steady, consistent work over dramatic ups and downs. You have a practical mindset and can spot potential issues early, but don't let this stop you moving forward with projects.
You appreciate clear guidelines and are naturally accountable for your work. You're more interested in finding the right solution than winning arguments, making sensible, well-considered decisions rather than jumping into things impulsively.

# Senior Legal Counsel, Privacy and Data Protection
* Full-time
## Company Description
At Nielsen, we are passionate about our work to power a better media future for all people by providing powerful insights that drive client decisions and deliver extraordinary results. Our talented, global workforce is dedicated to capturing audience engagement with content - wherever and whenever it’s consumed. Together, we are proudly rooted in our deep legacy as we stand at the forefront of the media revolution. When you join Nielsen, you will join a dynamic team committed to excellence, perseverance, and the ambition to make an impact together. We champion you, because when you succeed, we do too. We enable your best to power our future.
## Job Description
**This position can be done remotely within the UK. A central-London office is also available for hybrid work if preferred. You will be part of a friendly, international team.**
**Job Summary**
The Senior Legal Counsel, Privacy and Data Protection will provide sophisticated, practical, and business-oriented legal advice on EU/EEA privacy and data protection matters across Nielsen’s products, services, commercial relationships, and internal operations. This role will independently manage complex privacy workstreams, support Nielsen’s European privacy program, and serve as a trusted advisor to local sales and business teams. The role will work closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Information Security, Procurement, Sales, Marketing, and Legal colleagues across jurisdictions.
* Provide senior legal guidance on EU/EEA privacy compliance, data governance, and risk mitigation for business operations, products, partnerships, and commercial transactions.
* Apply in-depth knowledge and experience to solve complex privacy and commercial legal problems, using best practices and a practical understanding of Nielsen’s business.
* Work independently with minimal guidance, lead smaller projects and complex workstreams, and act as a resource for colleagues with less experience.
* Draft, review and negotiate complex data protection exhibits on both the buy-side and sell-side.
* Build consensus among stakeholders by explaining complex, difficult, or sensitive privacy and data protection issues in clear, actionable terms.
**Responsibilities**
* Provide day-to-day legal advice on the EU/EEA General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), applicable national implementing laws, European Data Protection Board (EDPB) guidance, supervisory-authority decisions, ePrivacy requirements, marketing and consumer protection rules, and other relevant European data protection and digital regulations.
* Maintain deep practical knowledge of EU/EEA privacy and data protection requirements and translate legal developments into clear, actionable guidance, contract language, policies, notices, processes, and implementation requirements for local and global stakeholders.
* Draft, review, and negotiate data processing agreements, data protection exhibits, data sharing and data use agreements, data transfer arrangements, and related privacy provisions in commercial contracts, representing Nielsen on both the buy-side and sell-side.
* Support local sales and business teams on privacy aspects of customer agreements, proposals, product offerings, data services, partnerships, and other commercial opportunities, providing timely and commercially practical advice.
* Conduct and oversee privacy impact assessments (PIAs/DPIAs), transfer impact assessments, legitimate interest assessments, and other privacy risk assessments for products, features, data uses, partnerships, and operational initiatives.
* Conduct privacy due diligence on third parties, vendors, customers, and strategic partners, including reviewing questionnaires and security materials, assessing processing activities and data flows, identifying gaps, negotiating remediation, and supporting ongoing oversight.
* Advise on advertising technology, audience measurement, analytics, identity, cookies, pixels, SDKs, targeted advertising, consent and preference management, data monetization, and related media and marketing data practices. Experience in adtech or media technology is strongly preferred.
* Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Information Security, Procurement, Sales, Marketing, and other stakeholders to assess proposed data collection, use, disclosure, retention, and deletion activities and to support compliant product launches and operational changes.
* Communicate with, or support communications with, local data protection authorities and other supervisory authorities as required, including in connection with regulatory inquiries, consultations, complaints, audits, filings, investigations, and data incidents.
* Support privacy incident and data breach response, data subject rights escalations, regulatory inquiries, audits, and other privacy compliance matters in coordination with local business teams, security, legal, and outside counsel.
* Contribute to and improve privacy program materials, including policies, procedures, playbooks, templates, training, records of processing, data inventories, data retention requirements, and compliance reporting.
* Monitor developments in EU/EEA and national privacy law, enforcement trends, and related digital regulation; assess their impact on Nielsen’s business and communicate recommendations to stakeholders.
## Qualifications
* Extensive experience practicing privacy, data protection, technology, commercial, or related legal work in-house, with a track record of producing high-quality independent work.
* Law degree or equivalent legal qualification; qualification or admission in the UK is required, consistent with the requirements for the role.
* Deep, practical knowledge of the GDPR and applicable national privacy and data protection laws in at least one relevant European jurisdiction, with the ability to apply requirements across products, contracts, and business processes.
* Demonstrated experience conducting or overseeing DPIAs/PIAs, transfer impact assessments, legitimate interest assessments, and privacy risk assessments, including documenting risks and tracking mitigations.
* Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating DPAs, data protection exhibits, and other privacy-related contract terms, including experience advising both buyers/customers and sellers/providers of data or services.
* Experience advising business, sales, product, technology, or commercial teams on complex privacy issues and translating legal requirements into practical, commercially workable solutions.
* Experience engaging with or supporting communications to supervisory authorities, regulators, or other public-sector stakeholders is preferred and may be required for certain matters.
* Strong legal research, writing, negotiation, analytical, and issue-spotting skills, with the ability to exercise sound judgment and build consensus among diverse stakeholders.
* Excellent written and verbal English communication skills; fluency in an additional European language is a plus.
**Preferred Qualifications**
* CIPP/E certification is greatly preferred, but it is not a hard requirement. CIPM, CIPT, or an equivalent privacy credential is also a plus.
* Adtech, martech, media measurement, audience analytics, data licensing, or digital advertising experience is strongly preferred.
* Knowledge of U.S. privacy and data protection requirements, including U.S. state privacy laws and the CCPA/CPRA, is an advantage.
* Knowledge of APAC privacy and data protection regulations—particularly India’s Digital Personal Data Protection framework, Australia’s Privacy Act and Australian Privacy Principles, or South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act—is an advantage.
* Familiarity with international data transfers, standard contractual clauses, cross-border data sharing, consent and preference management, privacy management tools, data mapping, and records of processing activities.
## Additional Information
**What can we offer you as an employee of Nielsen Media**
In addition to a competitive salary and benefits we offer a varied area of responsibility as well as an open corporate culture with numerous development opportunities. Above all, our employees appreciate the ability to work independently in a motivated and very friendly team. Social responsibility, open communication and living our values can be found not only on our homepage, but also in everyday work. An informal atmosphere in a dynamic media company with opportunities for ownership and personal development.

* ## About the Role
* This PhD project offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of the dosimetry standards that will support the next generation of cancer radiotherapy. The successful candidate will join a collaborative research programme between University College London (UCL) and the National Physical Laboratory (NPL), focused on establishing a robust dosimetry framework for Very High Energy Electron (VHEE) radiotherapy. VHEE radiotherapy is an emerging treatment modality that has the potential to transform cancer care through improved dose delivery to deep-seated tumours while reducing radiation exposure to surrounding healthy tissues. Despite its promise, there is currently no internationally established dosimetry protocol for VHEE beams. This project will address this critical challenge by developing, validating, and implementing accurate dosimetry methodologies traceable to primary standards. The student will work within a UKRI-funded Future Leaders Fellowship programme investigating dosimetry for advanced radiotherapy, including FLASH radiotherapy applications. The research will combine experimental measurements, detector characterisation, computational modelling, and international collaboration with leading accelerator and radiotherapy research facilities. Key responsibilities will include: Developing and evaluating reference conditions for VHEE dosimetry. Performing high-accuracy radiation measurements using calorimeters, ionisation chambers, and other advanced dosimetry systems. Investigating the performance of novel and commercially available radiation detectors in VHEE beams. Supporting experimental studies through Monte Carlo simulations and computational modelling. Contributing to research campaigns at national and international VHEE facilities. Analysing complex experimental data and disseminating research findings through scientific publications and conference presentations. Collaborating with leading experts in medical physics, dosimetry, metrology, radiation measurement, and radiotherapy. The student will be based within NPL's internationally recognised Radiation Dosimetry Group while maintaining strong links with UCL. This unique environment will provide access to world-class facilities, specialist instrumentation, and expertise in measurement science. The successful candidate will receive comprehensive training in radiation dosimetry, detector physics, computational methods, scientific communication, and project management, preparing them for a future career in academia, national laboratories, healthcare, or the wider radiation sciences sector. This PhD provides a unique opportunity to conduct impactful research at the forefront of medical physics and to help establish the measurement foundations required for the safe and effective clinical implementation of VHEE radiotherapy.
* ## About You
* We are seeking a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in medical physics, radiation dosimetry, and advanced radiotherapy technologies. The ideal applicant will have: A first-class or upper second-class degree (or equivalent) in Physics, Medical Physics, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related physical science discipline. A strong academic background in radiation physics, nuclear physics, medical imaging, particle accelerators, or related areas. An interest in experimental research and the development of novel technologies for healthcare applications. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex datasets and draw scientifically robust conclusions. Experience with scientific programming and data analysis (e.g. Python, MATLAB, C++, or similar tools) would be advantageous. Knowledge of Monte Carlo simulation techniques (e.g. Geant4, TOPAS, FLUKA, EGSnrc, or MCNP) is desirable but not essential. Strong practical laboratory skills and attention to detail, particularly in experimental measurements and instrumentation. An interest in radiation detectors, dosimetry systems, and measurement science. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical information clearly to scientific and non-specialist audiences. A willingness to travel for experimental campaigns at research facilities in the UK and Europe. Desirable, but not essential, experience includes: Previous research projects involving radiation measurements, detector development, medical physics, accelerator science, or computational modelling. Familiarity with ionization chambers, calorimetry, semiconductor detectors, or other radiation detection technologies. Experience in scientific publication, conference presentations, or collaborative research projects. Above all, we are looking for a curious, enthusiastic, and self-motivated individual who is excited by the opportunity to contribute to the development of international standards and dosimetry methodologies that will support the safe clinical implementation of Very High Energy Electron (VHEE) radiotherapy and FLASH radiotherapy. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the University College London (UCL) EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award (UELA) studentship scheme using the online application process. Applicants should apply via the UCL website (Project ID: 2531cs1075): https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/doctoral-school/funding/epsrc-doctoral-funding/epsrc-prospective-doctoral-students/ucl-epsrc-doctoral-landscape-award-uela-studentships Candidates are encouraged to review the eligibility criteria and application requirements on the UCL website before submitting their application. Applications submitted through other routes cannot be considered for this studentship. For informal enquiries about the project, prospective applicants may contact the supervisory team.

# Data Center Operations Implementation Manager

# **Role Overview**
We are seeking a Data Center Operations Implementation Manager to own the end-to-end Day 0 to Day 2 transition of Nscale's data centres — spanning construction, fit-out, and live, steady-state local operations — across an assigned region and set of sites. Rather than owning construction execution itself, you'll be the connective tissue between Construction, Network Engineering, Compute/Infrastructure Deployment, and local Operations teams — driving a structured, well-documented transition so every site goes live on schedule and ready to support production workloads. This is an individual-contributor role built on strong stakeholder management, cross-functional influence, and travel to sites during critical transition windows.
# **What You'll Do**
**Day 0 to Day 2 Transition Leadership**
* Own the end-to-end Day 0 to Day 2 transition process for each data centre site within your assigned region — spanning construction, fit-out, and steady-state operations.
* Define and maintain a standardized transition framework and readiness checklist applied consistently across your assigned sites.
* Track and drive closure of cross-team action items, dependencies, and blockers standing between construction handover and operational go-live.
* Identify and escalate risks to go-live timelines, and drive resolution across the relevant stakeholder groups.
**Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Coordination**
* Track progress and status across Construction, Network Engineering, Compute/Infrastructure Deployment, Facility Engineering, SDM, and local site Operations teams throughout the transition window.
* Partner with Construction teams to track handover status, outstanding items, and site readiness milestones.
* Track Network Engineering's buildout, testing, and cutover activities required for a site to go live.
* Track hardware intake, rack-and-stack, and deployment scheduling with Compute/Infrastructure Deployment teams to stay aligned with the transition timeline.
* Coordinate with Facility Engineering on site systems and infrastructure readiness ahead of transition.
* Engage with the Service Delivery Management (SDM) team to ensure alignment with customer needs, SLAs, security, and facility performance.
* Take part in regular cross-functional syncs and stakeholder reviews to stay current on transition status.
* Contribute to a shared sense of ownership and accountability across stakeholder teams, even without formal authority over them.
**Local Day Two Operations Readiness**
* Partner with local Operations leads to confirm staffing, training, tooling, and support processes are in place before a site transitions to Day 2 ownership.
* Create and validate standard operating procedures (SOPs) and operational processes required for local Operations teams to run the site post-handover.
* Create the operational site tool bill of materials (BOM) required for local Operations teams to maintain the site post-handover.
* Verify the spare parts bill of materials (BOM) is complete and in place ahead of Day 2 handover.
* Facilitate structured knowledge transfer and handover documentation from Construction, Network, and Compute teams to local Operations teams.
* Confirm monitoring, ticketing, and ITSM processes are validated and operating before a site is handed to local Operations.
* Act as an escalation point for local Operations teams during the early post-handover period to smooth the transition.
**Reliability, Safety & Compliance**
* Define and enforce Day 2 readiness criteria that a site must meet before transitioning to local Operations ownership.
* Facilitate root-cause analysis for transition delays or gaps surfaced during handover, and drive remediation across teams.
* Ensure health, safety, and environmental requirements are validated and documented as part of readiness sign-off.
* Support certification and audit readiness (ISO 27001, ISO 22237, SOC 2, Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 22301) ahead of go-live.
**Vendor & Supplier Coordination**
* Coordinate with construction contractors and colocation providers as needed to close out remaining items affecting the transition timeline.
* Track vendor commitments and SLAs relevant to the transition window, and escalate delays that put go-live at risk.
* Coordinate with the Supply Chain team to align hardware intake and staging with the transition schedule.
**Monitoring, Reporting & Analytics**
* Track KPIs and KRIs for the Day 0 to Day 2 transition process (time to transition, readiness checklist completion rate, post-handover incident rate, etc.).
* Build and maintain dashboards that track transition status across your assigned site pipeline for all stakeholder teams.
* Produce regular reports for senior leadership on transition status, risks, and blockers.
* Use data-driven insights to identify systemic bottlenecks in the Day 0 to Day 2 process and drive continuous improvement.
# **About You**
**Experience & Background**
* 3-8 years of experience in data centre operations, program/project management, or infrastructure deployment at scale.
* Proven track record coordinating the transition of new sites into live operations across construction, network, compute, and operations functions.
* Experience operating in a matrixed environment, influencing outcomes without direct authority over every stakeholder team.
* Demonstrated success managing multiple concurrent site transitions in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.
* Background in hyperscale, cloud, or HPC data centre environments (preferred).
**Technical Knowledge & Expertise**
* Working knowledge of data centre power, cooling, networking, and compute infrastructure, sufficient to coordinate effectively across specialist teams.
* Familiarity with network deployment and cutover processes, and compute/hardware deployment lifecycles.
* Knowledge of Layer 1 network infrastructure, including fiber, copper, optics, and transceivers.
* Familiarity with ITSM tooling, ticketing systems, and monitoring platforms used by local Operations teams.
**Influence & Communication**
* Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and align Construction, Network, Compute, and Operations teams without direct authority.
* Excellent cross-functional communication skills, able to translate technical detail between teams with different priorities and vocabularies.
* Program management discipline, with the ability to track and drive multiple concurrent workstreams to closure.
* Comfortable operating in ambiguous, matrixed, fast-moving environments.
* Bias toward ownership, pragmatism, and delivering results with urgency.
**Operational Excellence**

* Strong attention to detail in transition documentation and handover packages.

## Technical Estimator – Data Centres & Process Engineering
### Description
To provide technical and commercial estimating support across a broad range of engineered heating, cooling and process applications, with particular responsibility for supporting the continued growth of our Data Centre business.
The role will manage customer enquiries from initial receipt through to the preparation of technically compliant and commercially accurate proposals. This will involve engaging directly with customers, consultants and contractors to understand their requirements, interpreting technical specifications and drawings, identifying missing information, undertaking or coordinating engineering calculations, selecting and sizing appropriate equipment and developing suitable technical solutions.
The role will primarily cover fabricated pressure and storage vessels, including calorifiers, buffer vessels and specialist process vessels, together with heat exchangers, packaged heating and cooling systems, steam, condensate and associated mechanical equipment.
Customers and applications will span Data Centres, pharmaceutical, oil & gas, process engineering and other specialist industrial markets.
Following receipt of an order, the Technical Estimator will also be responsible for preparing a clear and comprehensive handover to Engineering, Design, Project Management, Procurement and Production.
**Person specification:**
* Strong technical aptitude with a good understanding of mechanical or process engineering principles.
* Technically curious and interested in understanding how a customer’s complete system operates rather than simply pricing a schedule.
* Numerate and comfortable undertaking engineering calculations.
* Methodical and accurate when dealing with specifications, calculations and pricing.
* Commercially aware and capable of balancing technical compliance, risk, cost and customer value.
* Confident questioning customers to obtain the information required to develop a solution.
* Able to interpret technical specifications, drawings, schematics and datasheets.
* Capable of identifying technical and commercial risks.
* Comfortable communicating with customers, consultants and engineers.
* Able to explain technical matters clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
* Able to manage multiple enquiries and competing priorities simultaneously.
* Proactive in obtaining missing information rather than relying on unsupported assumptions.
* Resourceful and willing to seek out the right person or information where required.
* Comfortable working autonomously and taking responsibility for progressing your own workload.
* Collaborative and comfortable working across Sales, Engineering and Manufacturing.
* Willing to take ownership and accountability for your work.
* Self-aware and willing to identify areas where additional knowledge, support or development would be beneficial.
* Computer literate and comfortable using Microsoft Word, Excel, email, internal business systems and electronic technical documentation.
### Essential Skills
Responsible for:
1. Managing technical and commercial enquiries across Data Centres, pharmaceutical, oil & gas, process engineering and other specialist markets.
2. Engaging directly with customers, consultants and contractors to establish their technical requirements, application and intended system operation.
3. Asking appropriate technical questions to identify missing information, clarify specifications and establish the design basis required to prepare an accurate quotation.
4. Reviewing specifications, schedules, datasheets, drawings, schematics and other technical documentation.
5. Identifying technical risks, ambiguities, exclusions and areas requiring further clarification before quotation.
6. Understanding the customer’s application and determining the most appropriate equipment or packaged solution.
7. Undertaking or coordinating engineering calculations required to size and select equipment, including calorifiers, buffer and storage vessels, specialist fabricated vessels, heat exchangers, packaged heating and cooling plant, pumps, valves, controls and associated equipment.
8. Interpreting operating temperatures, pressures, flow rates, heat loads and other relevant process parameters.
9. Understanding how individual components interact within the customer’s wider mechanical or process system.
10. Constructively challenging customer requirements where alternative solutions may improve performance, reliability, manufacturability, programme or value.
11. Producing accurate and commercially robust estimates covering materials, bought-out equipment, fabrication, assembly, testing, certification, documentation and other project requirements.
12. Obtaining and evaluating supplier quotations for specialist components, equipment and services.
13. Considering manufacturing complexity, programme, testing, inspection, certification and project-specific requirements when developing costs.
14. Preparing clear and professional technical and commercial proposals identifying scope, assumptions, exclusions, programme requirements and commercial terms.
15. Identifying opportunities for value engineering and alternative technical proposals where these may improve competitiveness or customer value.
16. Understanding relevant engineering standards, codes and regulatory requirements and recognising where specialist technical or compliance input is required.
17. Ensuring applicable testing, inspection, certification and documentation requirements are identified and included at enquiry stage.
18. Reviewing successful quotations and purchase orders to confirm that the order reflects the agreed technical and commercial scope.
19. Identifying and resolving discrepancies between quotations, specifications, correspondence and purchase orders before projects are released.
20. Preparing accurate order-entry information, bills of materials and supporting technical and commercial information.
21. Preparing comprehensive project handovers covering the agreed design basis, equipment selection, customer requirements, assumptions, exclusions, programme, testing and documentation requirements.
22. Providing clarification and technical support to Engineering, Design, Project Management, Procurement and Production following handover where required.
23. Working closely with the Data Centre Sales Lead and wider Sales team to qualify and prioritise opportunities.
24. Managing your own workload and priorities, taking ownership of progressing enquiries and contributing towards agreed performance measures.
25. Using the considerable technical knowledge available across the business effectively, knowing when to work through an issue independently and when to seek input from experienced colleagues.
### Desirable Skills
Previous experience within mechanical engineering, process engineering, HVAC, pressure equipment, heat transfer, packaged plant or a related engineered-product environment.
Experience or knowledge in several of the following areas would be advantageous:
* Technical estimating, proposals or applications engineering
* Customer-facing technical sales support
* Equipment sizing and selection
* Heat transfer principles and heat exchanger selection
* Pressure vessels and pressure systems
* Fabricated vessels and manufacturing processes
* Packaged heating and cooling plant
* Pumps, valves and associated mechanical equipment
* Steam and condensate systems
* Preparation of technical and commercial quotations
* Engineering standards and regulatory requirements
* Inspection, testing, certification and documentation requirements
* Supplier engagement and evaluation of bought-out equipment and services
* Project or engineering handover
Experience within Data Centres, pharmaceutical, oil & gas, industrial process, critical infrastructure or other technically demanding sectors would also be advantageous, but is not essential where the candidate can demonstrate strong transferable engineering capability.
### Qualifications
A qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Building Services Engineering, Process Engineering or a related discipline would be advantageous.
Equivalent practical engineering experience combined with strong technical knowledge and demonstrable capability will also be considered.
### Salary And Benefits
Competitive salary and benefits package.
Further details to be confirmed.
### Location
Bradford. The role will be predominantly Bradford office-based, with scope for flexible and home working where appropriate.
### Closing Date
16/11/2026

Education mental health practitioners work with schools and colleges to strengthen early support for children and young people. The work includes assessing presenting concerns, agreeing suitable interventions, monitoring progress and communicating with education staff and families within professional boundaries.
The Oxford team works across education and mental health services, so the practitioner needs to translate clinical knowledge into language that teachers, pastoral teams and families can use. Clear records, proportionate information sharing and reliable follow-up keep support coordinated around the young person.
## Clinical Practice And Partnership
A qualified EMHP uses structured, evidence-informed approaches for common mental health difficulties and supports prevention as well as early intervention. Each contact requires careful listening, a defined purpose and an agreed plan for the next stage of support.
Partnership work involves education professionals, mental health colleagues and other services. The practitioner contributes to discussions about risk, safeguarding, consent and onward referral, while keeping the young person's needs at the centre of decisions.

* Consultation with school and college staff

* Safeguarding and escalation of risk concerns

The post requires professional registration or qualification appropriate to the advertised EMHP role, together with the ability to work within NHS policies and local safeguarding arrangements. Practitioners maintain confidentiality, record decisions accurately and recognise when a concern needs a more specialist response.
Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust expects staff to work respectfully with children, young people, families and colleagues from different backgrounds. The role also requires reflective practice, supervision and continuing development as responsibilities change across education settings.
## Team-Based Mental Health Support
The practitioner works as part of a multidisciplinary service rather than in isolation. Regular communication helps the team coordinate referrals, allocate work, review outcomes and keep education settings informed about agreed actions.
Day-to-day work combines planned appointments, consultation and documentation. A dependable approach to diary management, case records and professional communication allows clinical time to remain focused on children and young people.
