We build frontier AI for environments where the cost of a wrong decision is high: defence and national security, critical infrastructure, and commercial organisations making high-stakes decisions on complex data. We are growing fast, and the constraint on how fast is no longer ideas or opportunity. It is whether the systems we ship are good enough for the people who stake decisions on them.
That is where you come in. We need engineers who can build the systems this mission depends on, and build them to a standard that holds when the answer has to be right. You will be trusted to own real systems end-to-end, held to a single high standard, and judged on one thing above all: whether what you ship earns the confidence people place in it when the decision matters.
If you are the kind of engineer who builds rather than assembles, who wants your work measured by whether it holds up in production rather than whether it demos well, and who wants to see the direct line from your code to systems people depend on, we would love to hear from you.

Founded in 2019, Oxford Dynamics is a fast-growing UK frontier technology company developing both digital and physical AI systems built to operate in dynamic, mission-critical environments.
At the core of everything we build is AVISTM (A Very Intelligent System), our orchestration platform: the intelligence layer that fuses multi-modal data, including text, imagery, telemetry and sensor feeds, so operators can interrogate complex information at speed and make better decisions under pressure. AVISTM powers our digital decision products, such as ORION for multi-source decision-to-effect, and it powers our physical platforms.
We work where wrong decisions can be catastrophic. We partner with defence, security and private sector organisations internationally to bring frontier AI into the environments where it matters most, whether that is protecting nations, infrastructure and lives, or transforming how commercial organisations reason over their data and make high-stakes decisions.
## Requirements
**About the role** This is a senior individual-contributor role with room to grow into staff-level scope. You will own significant parts of our platform end to end - design, build, ship, operate, and you will shape how the wider engineering team works: the architecture we converge on, the standards we hold, and the engineers we grow.
We care more about depth of engineering judgment than about any particular stack. Most of our backend is Python, our data lives in PostgreSQL, and everything ships in containers but if you have built serious systems elsewhere and want to work in this stack, we would still like to hear from you. **What you will be doing** **Systems and architecture (primary focus)**
· Design, build and evolve backend services for high-availability, high-throughput workloads – currently Python and FastAPI, though the principles matter more than the framework.
· Own the design of well-versioned HTTP APIs: clear contracts, consistency, idempotency, backward compatibility, and documentation people can actually use.
· Design event-driven systems and background processing pipelines (queues, streams, workers) that handle retries, partial failure and back-pressure gracefully.
· Model data properly and tune the databases behind it – schema design, indexing, query performance, migrations, and scaling strategy.
· Apply caching, rate limiting and queuing to hit explicit performance and latency budgets.
· Integrate with AI pipelines and model-serving endpoints, including streaming responses, async inference jobs, and sane error and retry semantics.
· Take on the ambiguous problems: the ones where the requirement is a paragraph, the constraints conflict, and someone needs to decide.

· Package and ship every service as a clean, minimal Docker container, with reproducible builds and sensible runtime defaults.
· Write secure, well-tested code – unit, integration and end-to-end, and raise the bar for others through code review.

· Take part in operating what we build – you should be comfortable being close to production.
**Technical leadership**
· Translate product intent into technical plans: milestones, sequencing, measurable success criteria, and honest estimates.
· Make trade-offs explicit and write them down, so the team can disagree with the reasoning rather than the conclusion.
· Mentor engineers on system design, API ergonomics and operational thinking; grow the people around you.
· Communicate clearly with stakeholders of varying technical background, including non-engineers and customers.
**Infrastructure (welcome, not required)**
· Contribute to infrastructure as code (Terraform/CloudFormation) and CI/CD (GitHub Actions/Argo CD) alongside the DevOps team.
· Support cloud operations with sensible defaults, cost awareness, and clean promotion across dev/staging/prod.
**Requirements Essential**
· Strong hands-on experience with Docker and containerised deployment – building images, debugging containers, and running containerised services in production.
· Strong programming ability in Python, or demonstrable depth in a comparable language with a willingness to work primarily in Python.
· A track record of building and operating production backend systems at a level where you set the design, not just implemented it.
· Proven experience designing and operating production APIs – versioning, security, documentation and automated testing.
· Solid grounding in relational database design, indexing, performance tuning and migrations (PostgreSQL or equivalent).
· Experience with asynchronous or event-driven architectures and the failure modes that come with them.
· Fluency with Git-based workflows and code review as a team practice.
**Nice to have**

· Exposure to enterprise data platforms (for example Palantir Foundry, Databricks or Snowflake).
· Observability tooling (Prometheus/Grafana, ELK/OpenSearch).

· Experience in regulated, safety-critical or security-cleared environments.

**How you work**
· High agency — you own outcomes end to end and pull on threads without being asked.
· Pragmatic and research-driven, with a bias to ship and iterate.
· A clear communicator, in writing as much as in conversation.

London, GBR
* Req ID: QDWrit/iBTEC/HospL3
We are currently recruiting for Subject Specialists to support the development of qualification content and materials for BTEC International Level 3 in Hospitality.
**Subject Specialist – QD Writer** **Purpose of this role:**
A Subject Specialist supports the creation and development of qualification content and materials for BTEC International Level 3 in Hospitality. Successful candidates will be expected to write the units assigned to them. Suitable individuals may also be invited to undertake additional activities by supporting the technical editing/reviewing of units within their chosen sector/subject area. We are looking for innovative writers with fresh ideas that motivate our learners and set them on the path to success. If you would like to be involved in shaping and developing our qualification content and assessment, apply now.
**Key Duties & Responsibilities**
**Writing activities**
● Write the required units and materials assigned according to the guidance provided
● Write clearly and concisely at Level 2 and Level 3 vocational standard
● Write assessment criteria as required
● Respond positively to feedback received
● Provide content in the required format using the specified format for submission
● Make amendments following feedback
● Produce accurate, relevant and engaging qualification content appropriate for the target learner cohort
● Technically edit/review units within the Hospitality sector/subject area, where required
● Follow the agreed brief and ensure materials meet the requirements of the qualification

● Provide up-to-date sector or subject-specific expertise that feeds into material production
● Keep up to date with changes in the sector/subject area
● Have detailed knowledge of the requirements/standards/specifications that encompass the role or area of expertise
● Have a good understanding of vocational qualifications within the Hospitality sector
● Meet deadlines & report back to Pearson within agreed timeframes
● Ensure parity of standards
● Adhere to guidance provided by Pearson
● Work effectively with colleagues
● Take part in training activities associated with the role, as required
**Background/Experience/Skills (Essential)**
● Have an understanding and experience of working within a vocational sector and/or have taught Hospitality or a relevant subject to learners aged 14-19
● Have a good understanding of vocational qualifications within the sector
● Have recent relevant teaching experience
● Have a relevant teaching qualification
● Have been educated to a Level 4 standard with relevant qualifications
● Be able to write at Level 2 and Level 3 vocational standard
● Have good written communication skills, particularly in the Hospitality sector/subject area
● Confident use of IT
● Have the ability to pick up new skills quickly and apply them, including the writing of assessment criteria
● Have the ability to follow a brief
● Be able to write clearly and concisely
● Have an ability to work to tight deadlines
**Background/Experience/Skills (Desirable)**
● Experience of writing educational materials and an ability to summarise materials and create engaging educational content

● Innovative writers with fresh ideas that motivate learners and support progression
● Experience in writing any of the following:
* support materials aimed at students, teachers and learning providers
* qualification units or specifications
* assessments or assessment criteria
* published or educational materials
* Experience providing feedback in a professional context
* Experience in qualification development, technical editing, reviewing or quality assurance activities

● Have a suitable broadband connection, microphone, headphones and a webcam
● Have a personal and secure email account
● Have the right to work in the UK

# Content Author for GCE A Level Pyschology
London, GBR
* Req ID: CA\_9PS0
As we continue to transition to a digital environment, we know that it’s essential to revisit and update our approaches to assessment delivery. Our aim is to create a more modern assessment delivery system that sets us up for the future, supports our Senior Associates better in their role by building associate capacity across the system, further supports our customers, and delivers the best outcomes for learners.
As part of a programme of modernisation, we are taking the opportunity to update our senior associate roles and responsibilities, across our qualifications.
We would like to offer you the opportunity to apply for one of these roles.
**Content Author for GCE A Level Psychology**
**About Pearson**
At Pearson we’re committed to a world that’s always learning. From bringing lectures vividly to life to turning textbooks into laptop lessons, we are always re-examining the way people learn best. We are bold thinkers and standout innovators who motivate each other to explore new frontiers in an environment that supports and inspires us to be better. By pushing the boundaries of technology, and each other to surpass these boundaries, we create seeds of learning that become the catalyst for the world’s innovations, personal and global. We are the UK's largest awarding body and offer qualifications that are globally recognised and benchmarked, with educational excellence rooted in a range of General and Vocational courses.
**Purpose**
The **Content Author** is there to produce error-free, factually accurate assessments that align with the subject specification.
**Core Services and Expectations**
When carrying out your role, please be mindful that you represent Pearson and that you should always maintain your professional integrity. Therefore, it is essential that you:
* Act at all times in a way which will not bring Pearson, its employees, and its representatives into disrepute.
* Read all Pearson policies and guidance prior to undertaking contracted activities.
* Respect the confidentiality of centres and learners.
* Attend any and all meetings or training sessions provided, relevant to your role, where requested by Pearson.
* Adhere to deadlines given by Pearson and ensure that all work is carried out to the best of an individual’s ability.
* Remain respectful and advocate for others to ensure and promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in a professional manner when carrying out services on behalf of Pearson.
* Have personal IT equipment capable of running Pearson software, relevant malware, appropriate virus protection software, a suitable internet connection, and a personal, secure email account.
* Communicate with Pearson and its centres in a timely manner when carrying out all designated responsibilities.
* Raise any concerns if you suspect or are made aware of any malpractice, maladministration, and/or safeguarding issues.
**Role Specific Services and Expectations**
As well as Pearson’s core services expectations, there are also role-specific services and expectations that you must consider and be able to provide. These include:
* Ensuring assessment materials comply with the Global Content Policy, fully support accessibility, diversity, equality, and inclusion, and sensitivity guidelines.
* Ensuring all applicable assessment materials produced are of high quality and show sufficient coverage of the assessment criteria as set out in the applicable assessment guidelines.
* Ensuring all materials are appropriate to the specific range of ability and will result in good discrimination and differentiation at all levels that it is designed to test.
* Advising on subject specialist matters throughout the production process and providing feedback where necessary.
* Adhering to the production schedules and turnaround requests, keeping Pearson informed of your availability which could affect deadlines.
* Ensuring that, where candidates may choose between questions, it can be demonstrated that any permitted combination of questions provides for the coverage of a similar balance of content and assessment criteria, where required.
* Producing assessment materials to ensure they meet the level of demand, and the questions are clear, fit for purpose, and error-free.
* Providing accurate sources used and, where applicable, so that Pearson can request copyright permission to use the material.
* Ensuring that appropriate graphics, photographs, diagrams, or images (where required) are from reputable sources and free from error.
* Ensuring that the nature and range of responses required by the mark scheme are appropriate and correct.
* Complying with the demands of the current specification as far as duration of the paper, reading/preparation time, number of questions/items, and all other aspects are concerned, and that the rubric is clear and reflects these requirements.
* Ensuring that materials do not contain unnecessary repetition of questions and that distractors do not inform the answer to other questions.
* Reviewing, reporting, and clearly marking up comments and producing revised assessment materials, as and when required, throughout the production process.
* Providing feedback on drafts at each stage and attending sign-off meeting(s) where required.
* Ensuring all associated materials are updated throughout the production process.
* Signing off the final assessment material.
* Supporting, reviewing, and agreeing on modified paper amendments, where requested by Pearson.
**Experience and Qualifications required:**
**Experience:**
As a representative of the company, you will be expected to have experience in, or be able to demonstrate the ability of the following:
* Excellent communication skills.
* In-depth knowledge and understanding of the specific content area (e.g., assessments and curriculum development).
* Proven ability to provide and co-ordinate training.
* Proven track record of leading quality assurance activities.
**Qualifications:**
Qualifications required to apply for your chosen role at Pearson will depend on the qualification you are delivering. Please contact Pearson ahead of your application if the requirements are not clear.

* Degree or equivalent qualifications in Psychology
* Experience in teaching GCE A Level Psychology
* A UK recognised teaching qualification
* Subject knowledge - Demonstrates deep knowledge of the specification, including its content, structure, and assessment requirements.
Please note upon successful application Pearson may ask you to provide proof of the qualifications required.

You'd be deciding what it should be, then building it.
For additional context, our tech stack currently include: GCP, BigQuery, dbt Core, Airflow, SQL, Python, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot.
# Who you'll work with
You'll report to the Data Engineering Manager who oversees the Data Infra & MLOps team as well as the Data Services & Governance team. The goal is one canonical definition of Monthly recurring revenue (MRR), churn, transaction, customer - used by analysts, BI tools, and AI tools without divergence. You make that real, not aspirational.
* Set data modelling standards for the function: what clean, layered, well-tested dbt architecture looks like across all domains, at all levels of complexity.
* Build and run the Analytics Engineering community of practice including code reviews, shared patterns, documentation, onboarding etc. The goal is to create a social infrastructure that makes standards stick.
* Own the AI-native development practice. Use AI coding tools as a native part of how you write, review, and migrate data models (not as a demonstration, but as your actual workflow). Evaluate what works in a governed data engineering context, what introduces risk, and shape how the Analytics Engineering community adopts it.
* Lead responsible AI-augmented migration work using AI tooling to accelerate data modelling and migrations across the Analytics Warehouse and Operational Data Platform.
* Design data models and metric definitions in a documented and structured manner enabling reliable consumption by AI services without human intervention.
* Engage upstream with backend and product engineers to drive data contract discipline and schema ownership upstream, rather than managing inconsistency downstream.
* Contribute to Data & AI Products for external customer-facing analytics where data modelling patterns and conversational analytics needs and capabilities grow.
# What you bring
* Deep demonstrated expertise in dbt and modelling practices: not just strong modelling, but a formed view of what modelling architecture should look like across a function. You can defend trade-offs, teach them, and enforce them in teams you don't manage.

* Real experience owning a semantic layer (LookML, dbt MetricFlow, or equivalent). You have a point of view on what metric consistency should look like at scale, what breaks when it doesn't, and how to design it so AI tooling can consume it without degrading trust.
* AI-native development practice in a data engineering context. You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or equivalent) as a genuine part of how you work, and you can be specific about where they add real value and where they introduce risk in a governed analytics codebase.
* A track record of setting standards across teams you don't directly manage and making them stick by leveraging effective influencing techniques as opposed to relying on authority.
* Understanding of what LLMs and agentic tools need from a data layer such as how to model data, write documentation, and define metrics so that AI tools get consistent answers at runtime.
* Proven experience engaging credibly with backend engineers on data contracts and with senior stakeholders on what the semantic layer strategy means for the business.

This role is a good fit if:
* You can hold a standard without needing it applied perfectly, and you know which compromises are fatal and which are just untidy.
* You genuinely enjoy growing a community of practice through influence rather than authority and you take pride in seeing colleagues adopt and grow standards.
* You find the "how do we make data legible to an agent, not just to an analyst" problem interesting in its own right, rather than as a trend to keep up with.

* You want to own a domain. The Intelligence teams have strong AEs doing that. This role is for someone who wants to own the standards they build to.

* You are more comfortable being consulted than being accountable. The semantic layer and modelling standards you set have downstream consequences across the whole function and in AI features customers use.

We want someone who loves figuring out how complex software works from the outside, can reverse-engineer black-box behaviour, and turn their discoveries into reliable, production-grade integrations.
## The challenge
We integrate with legacy Electronic Health Record (EHR) platforms, many built over 20 years ago on Oracle/PL-SQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and other legacy enterprise backends.
Behind these internal application APIs are complicated stored procedures, hidden server-side session state, inconsistent validation, and limited transactional guarantees.
We build Chrome browser extensions that use an authenticated user's session to interact with the same APIs used by the official EHR web application. A seemingly simple operation, such as creating a patient or saving a clinical note, can involve 10 or more dependent API calls.
**The hardest part is not making the happy path work (although that isn't always easy). It's anticipating everything that could go wrong.**
Without documentation or vendor support, you'll be responsible for proactively identifying and mitigating failure scenarios across long, stateful chains of operations: partial writes, unexpected server state, concurrency, duplicate records, interrupted requests, and subtle data-integrity issues. You'll need to reason about what the system might be doing internally, test your hypotheses, and design integrations that fail safely when assumptions don't hold.
## What we're looking for
**Real experience reverse-engineering software interfaces and building working integrations against undocumented APIs is our strongest requirement.**
We're particularly interested in engineers who have built connectors into legacy systems by investigating how their existing applications communicate with their backends, rather than consuming officially supported, documented APIs.
Relevant experience might include:
* **Online travel booking:** Automating booking portals, travel-agent applications, or complex GDS workflows, particularly through reverse-engineered APIs, browser extensions, or browser-based automation.
* **Payroll and HR connectivity:** Building integrations into payroll providers or workforce platforms through undocumented web interfaces.
* **Insurance:** Automating legacy carrier portals, quoting systems, policy administration, or claims workflows.
* **Banking and financial connectivity:** Reverse-engineering online banking interfaces, account aggregation, or complex financial transaction workflows.
* **Other legacy enterprise software:** Building unsupported connectors, automation, or interoperability layers for complex, stateful applications.
**The scale or commercial success of the project matters far less than what you personally figured out and built.** Relevant experience could come from a substantial hobby project, an independent experiment, a one-person commercial product, or an engineering team.
You'll also need:
* Strong JavaScript/TypeScript, HTTP, browser, and modern web application fundamentals.
* Experience or strong familiarity with Chrome extensions, browser APIs, and session management.
* Exceptional analytical reasoning, resourcefulness, and an ability to infer complex system behaviour from limited evidence.
* Deep attention to correctness, concurrency, partial failures, and data integrity.
* The ability to produce maintainable software while moving exceptionally quickly.
* Proactivity and agency.
* To be comfortable and happy with full ownership over integration.
* Strong passion towards mental health and the company's mission.
* Strategic planning around design and ability (or strong willingness) to anticipate diverse user behaviors.
* Almost obsessive enthusiasm and interest in your field of work with the strong, continuous desire to improve.
* To be comfortable with an early stage, high-velocity, quickly changing start up environment and work independently with minimal managerial oversight.
* To have the ability to reflect, admit your mistakes, own them, learn from them and bounce back stronger.
* To care - about your work, impact and colleagues.
* Willingness to learn HIPAA requirements and handle protected health information carefully.
* Able to travel to the US for business when needed.
## How we work
**We are a high-velocity engineering team.** Our ambition is to build, in months, integrations that would traditionally take years to deliver in healthcare.
We're looking for someone who combines deep technical curiosity with urgency and execution. Someone equally comfortable with modern application architecture and the messy realities of legacy enterprise systems, who challenges assumptions, experiments rapidly, and finds creative ways around difficult technical constraints without compromising correctness.
We expect you to be **highly proficient with modern AI-assisted engineering tools**, using them to accelerate research, reverse engineering, implementation, testing, and iteration while independently validating their outputs.
We believe software engineering is changing fundamentally. We want someone who recognises that change, embraces emerging tools and techniques, and wants to help define what highly effective software engineering looks like over the next few years.

# Verification, Validation and Test Engineer
**About Rimac Energy**
Rimac Energy is a rapidly growing division of Rimac Group, developing next-generation battery energy storage and power conversion technology for grid-scale and commercial energy applications. Building on Rimac’s expertise in battery systems, power electronics and software, we are developing highly integrated BESS and PCS products for deployment across global markets, with an initial focus on the United States followed by Europe.
We are seeking an experienced Verification, Validation and Test (VVT) Engineer to take ownership of test engineering for our energy storage products. You will plan and run verification and validation campaigns, own failure analysis, and make sure every test produces the traceable evidence needed for certification. This role carries forward established test methods and knowledge through a structured handover, so you will join early enough to learn the existing rigs, procedures and certification approach before taking full ownership. The ideal candidate combines hands-on test experience with high-voltage battery and power electronics systems, a disciplined approach to evidence, and a passion for sustainable energy.
**Key Responsibilities:**
* Own the verification and validation test plans for products, from requirements and test specifications through to final reports.
* Take over and maintain the certification test methods, keeping procedures, test cases and acceptance criteria current and repeatable.
* Carry out performance, reliability, safety and environmental testing on battery, power electronics and system-level hardware.
* Lead failure analysis and root-cause investigations, working with design, integration and software teams to close issues and confirm fixes through retest.
* Produce clear, auditable test evidence and reports that support certification submissions and technical files, working closely with the Compliance Engineer.
* Maintain traceability between requirements, test cases and results so that test outcomes can be shown against the relevant standards.
* Define rig, fixture and instrumentation requirements, and direct test technicians in rig preparation, safe operation and data collection.
* Develop and improve test automation and data analysis using tools such as Python and LabVIEW.
* Support testing at external certification laboratories and test facilities, and act as a technical point of contact during witness testing.
* Communicate test progress, risks and results to engineering leads and programme stakeholders.
**Qualifications & Experience:**
* Bachelor's degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
* Proven experience in verification, validation or test of battery energy storage systems, power electronics or similar high-voltage products.
* Experience producing test evidence for product certification, and familiarity with relevant standards (for example IEC 62619, IEC 62477, UL 1973 / UL 9540 or grid codes).
* Strong failure analysis and root-cause problem-solving skills (for example 8D, fishbone or fault tree analysis).
* Strong understanding of test methodologies, instrumentation, data acquisition and monitoring tools.
* Experience with test automation and scripting, ideally Python and/or LabVIEW.
* Safe working practices for high-voltage systems; HV qualification or willingness to obtain one.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a disciplined approach to documentation.
* Desirable: experience of a test lab handover or building up a test function, and of directing technicians.
**What we are like and what we offer**
* **Technically challenging, high-impact work** on advanced energy storage and power conversion products — from concept through prototype, validation, and production
* **A collaborative, cross-functional engineering culture** with strong links between mechanical, electrical, controls, software, compliance, CAE, test, supply chain, and manufacturing
* **Fast-paced environment** where practical problem-solving and initiative are genuinely valued
* **Continuous learning and development**, with exposure to rapidly evolving energy and power electronics technology
* **A friendly, ambitious team** that works hard and takes pride in what it builds
* **Educational budget –** at Rimac Energy, we believe in the importance of continuous learning. We provide an educational budget to support your growth, and we actively encourage you to expand your knowledge and skills.
* **Pet-friendly workplace** – we are always on the lookout for new Pawject Managers! You’ll be able to bring your pet to work.

# Cat Fosterer (Blackberry Farm Animal Centre HP22 4RJ AYLESBURY)
We are looking to recruit cat and kitten fosterers for some of the animals in our care. Some cats, who are waiting to be rehomed, don’t respond well to cattery life and thrive much better in the care of a quiet foster home. Other cats looking for foster homes may be subject to an RSPCA investigation so are in our care whilst the case progresses. With these cats we will not know how long the case will take to resolve and, in rare cases, animals may have to be returned to their owner (in accordance with court ruling).
For whatever reason the cat has come into our care, being in a home environment is far more beneficial to their welfare for many reasons, such as medical issues or behavioural problems (very nervous) or if they are pregnant or nursing mothers or kittens which need additional care and are simply too young to rehome.
As a cat fosterer you will play a vital role in looking after the cats in our care until their case is resolved or they find a new home. You'll be fostering cats in your own home and ensuring a safe environment that will cater for their individual (and sometimes complex) needs. This will include allowing them to take the time to become accustomed to their new surroundings and people in those surroundings, feeding them and taking them to a vet (as required, with costs will be covered by the RSPCA). The care and interaction you will provide will help the cats in your care develop the socialisation skills which can aid a successful rehoming.
This is a great opportunity to make a real difference to the welfare of cats. Having animals in foster homes help us help more animals by freeing up space in our Centres and Branches.
What is required:
* Be able to transport the cat/kittens to Vet appointments if needed
* Have time to spend with them or be around for them
* A spare room at home or a quiet space for fostering a cat (they will not be allowed outside of your home environment, so would need a specific space)
* Have lots of love, time and patience to give the animal whilst they are with you.
We’re looking for experienced cat people who have owned or fostered cats before, and understand their behaviours and needs. All necessary equipment, and Veterinary care will be supplied and funded by the RSPCA.You will have the support of our staff on hand should you need it.
To apply, please complete our application form which will ask you to expand on your experience and home environment. Our application process is very thorough as fostering is a very responsible but rewarding role. It may take up to 30 minutes to complete the application, so make sure you have a cup of tea to hand as you complete it.
If successful, you’ll be added to our team of fosterers who can be contacted by any of our National Centres or Branches looking for the right person with the right skills to support a particular cat. You’ll get online access to all the necessary training for your role and we ask you to keep this up to date. We have a suite of wellbeing resources available and can make reasonable role adjustments to support you in your volunteering.
We celebrate and respect the diversity of our RSPCA team and embrace the individual qualities, skills and experiences that everyone brings.
Please note you need to live within an hour of the centre HP22 4RJ.

### ## **Role Overview**
The Enterprise Customer Success Manager owns Sedna's most commercially significant customer relationships. This is a senior, largely autonomous role for someone who is equally comfortable running an executive-level conversation and building the account infrastructure, success plans, health monitoring, renewal strategy, that makes that conversation credible.
The portfolio spans Premier and Strategic accounts globally. These are customers with high ARR, high complexity, and in many cases, long relationships that carry both genuine opportunity and genuine risk. The job is to hold those relationships well, act on signals before they become problems, and surface and progress commercial outcomes in partnership with Sales.
This is not a role that fits someone who needs clear direction on what to do next. The expectation is that you read the account, form a view, and act on it. The Head of Customer Success is there for strategic decisions and unusual situations, not routine account management.
## **Key Responsibilities**
### **Account Ownership**
* Own a named portfolio of Premier and Strategic accounts. Know them well enough that no renewal, no escalation, and no expansion conversation comes as a surprise.
* Build and maintain executive-level relationships. The relationship should not depend on the product working perfectly; it should be strong enough to hold when it does not.
* Produce and execute success plans tied to customer outcomes, not just product usage metrics. Plans should reflect what the customer is trying to achieve and how Sedna is contributing to it.
* Run QBRs with commercial framing. A QBR should advance the relationship and the commercial position, not just report on the quarter.
* Maintain deep product knowledge across Sedna Email, Prefix, and VMS. You are not delivering training, but your commercial conversations need to be grounded in a genuine understanding of how customers are using the product and where they are not.
### **Retention and Renewal**
* Monitor account health continuously and act on risk signals before they become churn conversations. If a customer is at risk, the Head of Customer Success should hear about it from you, not from the customer.
* Co-own the renewal conversation with the AE. Own the preparation, the relationship context, and the customer's readiness to renew; Sales owns the close.
* Escalate renewal risk early, with a clear view of what is driving it and what the options are.
### **Growth and Expansion**
* Identify and progress expansion opportunities in collaboration with the AE. This means having enough commercial awareness to spot the signal and enough credibility with the customer to explore it.
* Bring the Head of Customer Success into complex or large deals at the right moment, not after the conversation has already been shaped.
### **Cross-functional Coordination**
* Coordinate training delivery through Education. You are not responsible for delivering training; Education owns that. Your job is to ensure the right training reaches the right accounts at the right time.
* Work with the Programme Manager to ensure smooth onboarding for new accounts entering the portfolio.
* Provide context to Education Specialists before training sessions on Premier and Strategic accounts, so delivery is appropriately calibrated.
* Partner with Support and Product to close feedback loops and ensure customer insights are informing the right internal conversations.
## **About You**
* Significant experience managing complex, high-value B2B accounts at a senior level, with a track record of holding executive relationships and co-owning commercial outcomes alongside Sales.
* Strong executive presence and the ability to hold a relationship through difficult conversations, not just good ones.
* A background in shipping, maritime operations, or global trade is strongly preferred. Sedna serves some of the world's largest maritime businesses, and candidates who understand how those organisations operate will be better placed to build credible, lasting relationships with them.
* Commercially fluent: able to read a renewal situation, understand what is driving it, and act with appropriate urgency without waiting to be asked.
* Clear, structured communicator in writing and in person, comfortable presenting to senior stakeholders and leading commercial conversations.
* Familiarity with Salesforce or equivalent CRM. Experience with tools such as Mixpanel or Snowflake is an advantage.
## **What Success Looks Like**
* A portfolio where no renewal, escalation, or expansion conversation comes as a surprise, because you have been managing the signals well in advance.
* Executive relationships on Premier accounts that are strong enough that customers would describe you as genuinely useful, not just present.
* Net Revenue Retention at or above target, with a clear understanding of what drove the result in both directions.
* Expansion pipeline contribution in partnership with Sales, with opportunities identified and progressed rather than waited for.
* Customer insights flowing consistently into QBRs, product feedback, and internal planning.
## **Directional KPIs**
* Net Revenue Retention on portfolio
* Logo retention rate on portfolio
* Expansion ARR generated
* Renewal on-time rate
* QBR completion rate against plan
* Time to escalation on at-risk accounts (faster is better)
* Executive relationship health, qualitative, assessed quarterly by Head of Customer Success
* Training coordination rate: proportion of accounts receiving at least one Education touchpoint per quarter

Finally, culture is important to us, so we also look for candidates who share our values:
### **Stay Ahead, Stay Agile**
* We don’t just adapt-we anticipate change and act with confidence.

* By staying open to new ideas and ways of working, we lead the future.

## What you'll be doing
As our Senior Occupational Psychologist (Product & Skills Science), you'll help define what assessment looks like in an AI-native world. This is a senior individual contributor role for a deep specialist who wants to turn skills science into products that change how the world hires.
You'll work directly with our Co-Founder, Nick Shaw, to set the scientific direction for our assessments. You'll define the principles behind them and work with our Data Science team to turn them into scalable, data-driven products. You'll champion rigorous, evidence-led approaches so our assessments are fair, predictive and effective at launch, and so they keep improving as they learn from more data.
You'll join a fast-moving, AI-native company that's rethinking assessment from first principles. Success in this role means combining scientific rigour with curiosity, pragmatism and a bias for action, and building new forms of assessment that stand up to scrutiny and deliver results in the real world.

* Shape the scientific foundations of a new generation of assessments, owning the skills science principles that determine what we measure and how we uncover the signals that matter

* Build the evidence behind assessment innovation, leading ongoing validation to demonstrate reliability, fairness and predictive power as our products evolve
* Make the science behind our products clear and credible through rigorous technical reports and manuals that give our teams and clients confidence in the results
* Turn assessment data into product breakthroughs, using statistical analysis to uncover insights and translate them into better assessment design and scoring
* Bring our science to life with clients, supporting validation and research alongside colleagues across the business to show how our assessments perform in the real world

## Location
London
## Employment Type
Full time
## Location Type

## Department
Commercial

OverviewApplication
In just over two years, we’ve gone from 0 to over 900 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. We’re now on the hunt for a brilliant growth marketer who wants to make an enormous impact on Spruce’s growth trajectory as we add thousands of installers over the next 18 months. You’ll help to scale and own our marketing and growth engine – campaigns, content, ads, and the experiments that tell us what’s actually working – and generally anything that helps accelerate our growth.
This is not an easy job – but we can promise it’ll be incredibly stimulating & fulfilling, and you’ll struggle to find a lovelier, more engaged group of customers to work with (..and the team’s not bad either!).
## 🌲 About Spruce
* Almost 20% of the UK’s carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there’s simply no way to make reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But there’s a problem: the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it really hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can’t currently offer a heat pump when someone’s boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.
* We’re fixing this. We’ve built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we’re having a massive impact on hundreds of installation businesses, merchants, utilities and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job, doubling their sales conversion rates, and boosting their bottom line.
* We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and have been scaling the team to massively grow our impact. We’re in the process of expanding outside heat pumps and by the end of the year will be an operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and autoCAD, you might get a sense of where we’re headed...
## 🥖 The Role
As we drive the business towards the next fundraise, you’ll be working closely with Hector and our founder Jo, to scale our growth engine. No two days will be the same, but at minimum your work will include:
* **Running growth experiments** – setting up and running our full set of growth/marketing tests across. This involves anything that can get the product into the hands of more users, quickly binning things that don’t work, and iterating quickly on everything to find our growth levers.
* **Creating & managing ads, creative, and content** – top and middle-funnel marketing content, videos, customer testimonials, short form copy for our website, socials, ads, and nurturing emails, and onboarding guides for new customers.
* **Owning our distribution channels** – partnerships, website, socials, email nurture, paid ads and events, making sure each one is pulling its weight and the pipeline it generates is handed cleanly to sales.
* **Marketing analytics & reporting** – breaking down conversion rates through our marketing and sales pipelines, tracking CAC and channel performance, spotting areas we can improve, and coming up with suggestions for when and how we should change tack.
* **Making sales yourself** – we care about doing whatever has the most impact on growth. The role sits inside the wider commercial team, so when that means jumping into sales calls or closing leads yourself, we need someone who sees that as part of the job, not a distraction from it.
## 🫵 About You
You'll have somewhere between 2 and 5 years of work experience. You don't need a marketing background, but you do need to show us you can spot opportunities and push things forward, whether that's campaigns you've run, content you've created, or projects where you've built something from scratch and got it in front of people. You'll ideally be:
* **Relentlessly proactive** — you naturally take responsibility, are always pushing to make things better, and just want to crack on and get sh\*t done;
* **A brilliant communicator** — you write compelling, concise copy and can explain complex concepts simply;
* **Full of creative energy** — you have ideas for how to get more installers onto Spruce and you can't wait to test them. You look at what other companies have done well and think about how to adapt it, not copy it;
* **Hands-on with the tools** — you’re willing to roll-up your sleeves to run campaigns yourself across paid ads, email and socials, and you’re comfortable building landing pages, setting up tracking, and making content without waiting for someone else to do it;
* **Data-minded** — you're comfortable pulling apart a funnel to work out where it's leaking and you know your way around a spreadsheet, but you use data to decide what to try next, not as a substitute for ideas;
* **A natural "people person"** — you love working with people and have a natural interest in their problems. You find it easy to warm to them and quickly put them at ease;
* **Genuinely curious about our customers** — heat pump installers are small business owners doing technically complex, physically demanding work. The best marketing we can do starts with understanding their world, and you'll spend real time talking to them;
* **An AI whizz** — you’re way ahead of the average person with your LLM usage, have built interesting/cool things in your spare time, and are deeply conscious of all the things that are possible that you haven’t had a chance to try yet;
... and you’ll hopefully also love heat pumps! 🤓
## 🌟 Our Offer
* 💰 Base salary £50-70k, with quarterly bonus aligned to company targets
* 🍰 Slice of equity (options) in the company
* 🏖️ 33 days holiday and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year
* 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme (YellowNest)
* 🏥 Private Medical Cover
* 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave
* 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme
* 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow
* 🌍 Meaningful, impactful work that genuinely improves the world.
## 🧑‍💻 Working At Spruce
* We’re currently a close-knit team of 32, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2-3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone altogether every fortnight.
* You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.
* We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then be able to rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions.
* We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it, what can we learn and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.
* Feedback is constant, direct, and kind – we'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.

**Hello. We’re Teya.**
Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you
**The role** The Retention & Recovery Lead owns one pipeline that follows every merchant from the first sign they might leave, through retention, a well-run exit and collections, to write-off or debt sale. Today we treat churn and collections as separate problems, and neither has a clear owner. In practice they are usually the same merchant at different points in time: a merchant who goes quiet in March becomes, by June, an unpaid fee, a terminal still in the field and a balance nobody is chasing. Collections activity also sits in pockets across the business, from unpaid subscriptions and fees, negative balances and chargebacks to terminal recovery, dissolved companies and fraud losses. As our credit products grow, so will the need. You’ll bring all of this together under one strategy, one queue and one set of metrics. We want someone who knows collections and its pain points, and who approaches the whole lifecycle with a product and design mindset: redesigning journeys end to end, and deciding where AI and automation belong and where people add the most value. You’ll start hands-on and build a small credit control team as the capability grows. **What you’ll do**
* Own the retention-to-recovery pipeline end to end, from the first churn signal to write-off or debt sale, running from one prioritised queue with one set of definitions.
* Work with our data team to build and run an AI retention engine that identifies merchants heading towards churn, recommends the next best action for each and puts them in a queue to be worked. Prove what works with holdout groups, and do more of it.
* Agree with Commercial how save conversations are delivered, and make sure our own risk actions, such as held settlements, are weighed before they push a good merchant out.
* Design a proper exit for every merchant who leaves: a recorded reason, fees stopped, terminal returned, final balance netted and a final statement, so merchants do not need to contact Customer Relations to close their account.
* Build automated collections that start the day a balance turns negative: settlement netting, direct debit, card on file, payment links and payment plans. Journeys run through the Teya app and portal first, with phone as the exception.
* Run managed and external recovery for larger balances: credit control, payment plans, an agency panel, write-off thresholds and, as a last resort, debt sale.
* Own the recovery strategy for fraud-related balances with Fraud Operations and Legal. They keep investigation and legal action; you make sure every balance has a recovery route and a priority.
* Run the existing book as a separate remediation project with its own end date, so it does not pull focus from the new flow.
* Connect the work of Billing, Payments, Logistics (terminal recovery), Credit, Customer Relations and the termination and withheld funds process into one joined-up flow.
* Define and own the pipeline’s metrics, report them monthly, and feed what you learn back into onboarding, pricing and risk policy.
* Prepare the capability to scale with Teya’s growing credit book, and hire and lead the credit control team.
**What success looks like** **In your first six months**
* Definitions agreed and reported for flow recovery rate, stock recovery rate and true churn.
* A single queue live, worked by hand from simple rules while the model is built.
* An exit process in place for every leaving merchant, and an automated collections first version running in at least one market.
* The credit control team hired or in hiring, and the legacy book project under way with a clear plan.
**By the end of your first year**
* The first retention model live, beating the rules-based baseline and tested against holdout groups.
* Flow recovery rate by day 90 tracking towards our 70% target, with time to recovery and cost to collect reported monthly.
* The first debt sale completed, where the legal and data preconditions are met.
* Measurably fewer Customer Relations contacts from merchants who are leaving or owe us money.
**What you’ll bring**
* Hands-on collections or recovery experience at some point in your career, ideally with small businesses, covering payment plans, agencies and write-offs, so you know where the pain points sit.
* Experience with retention, churn or customer lifecycle work, or a clear view of how retention and collections connect.
* A strong product mindset: you think in journeys, systems and outcomes, not only operational volume.
* A track record of designing, rolling out and running new processes, shipping a working first version quickly and improving it.
* A practical, curious approach to AI and automation, with the judgement to know where they help and where they don’t.
* Comfortable with data: defining metrics, working with data scientists on models and reading the results of tests and holdouts.
* A sound grasp of fair treatment and regulation in collections: treating small businesses fairly, spotting vulnerability, applying Consumer Duty principles where they apply, and knowing why we never contact a merchant under AML or fraud review.
* Experience in a smaller, fast-moving company such as a start-up, scale-up or fintech. Experience at larger organisations is welcome alongside this.
* Strong stakeholder management across Risk, Commercial, Finance, Billing and Legal, and the ability to get teams behind one approach.
* A clear, confident communicator in writing and in person, highly motivated and able to work independently.
**Nice to have**
* Experience of debt sale or forward-flow agreements.
* Collections across several European markets.
* Experience with credit products such as cash advance or lending.

# Gameplay Programmer
### Gameplay programmers build the systems a player touches directly: movement, combat, abilities, progression and the rules that hold them together.
Gameplay programming turns a design document into something that runs. The work covers character control, combat, abilities, AI hooks, UI plumbing and the state that has to survive a session or a patch. Most of it happens in C++ or C#, inside Unreal or Unity, and a good part of the job is iteration: a designer wants a mechanic to feel different, and the loop from change to playable build has to stay short.
Performance comes with the territory. A feature that works in isolation still has to fit a frame budget on the target hardware, which is why profiling, memory behaviour and data layout appear in postings at every seniority level. On live games the same systems need backward compatibility, because saved player state outlives any single release.
The line to an engine programmer runs along ownership: engine work serves every feature equally, gameplay work serves one feature as well as possible. Technical designers sit on the other side, closer to tuning than to code.

### A data scientist in games builds models from player data: what predicts churn, which matchmaking change helps, where an experiment result is real and where it is noise.

Python and SQL are the everyday tools, with machine learning where a prediction is genuinely needed rather than as a default. Experiment design, A/B testing and statistical reasoning carry at least as much weight as model building, because most of the damage in this field comes from confident conclusions drawn from thin evidence.
A Data Analyst answers defined questions and keeps reporting running. A Data Engineer builds the pipelines the data arrives through. The data scientist works on the questions that have no agreed method yet.

## About Thunk
We’re a small Digital Innovation company, mostly remote, occasionally Kings Cross, London. We work across all sorts of innovation projects; climate infrastructure, healthcare systems, emerging tech. We’re deep into what we do. So deep, that we’re quietly very good at it.
We need someone to help us take things even deeper.
## **Your work**
You’ll be Thunk’s lead developer: the person who owns how we build, not just what gets built.
Most of your week goes on our flagship climate project. You’ll lead its frontend and work directly with the client and partner teams.
The rest goes across Thunk: prototypes we test with real users, our own products and internal tools.
As we grow, you’ll shape Thunk’s engineering — standards, tooling, infrastructure and, in time, the developers who join after you.
Day-to-day, you’ll work closely with the whole team. Nine people, so the org chart is more of an org sentence. We’re a close, friendly bunch. Small team, real ownership, a short line to decisions.
## The flagship project
Most of your time goes on a climate resilience platform for UK infrastructure. It helps network operators understand how climate threats spread across connected systems.
It’s a long-running, multi-phase programme delivered by a consortium. Thunk designs and builds the frontend; partner teams own the backend, data and hosting.
* Frontend: Next.js with IBM’s Carbon Design System
* Data: partner APIs, a knowledge graph and GeoServer map data
* Code and delivery: GitLab with CI/CD pipelines
* Auth: Keycloak
* Releases: feature branches, merge requests, tagged release candidates, then production
* Environments: six — dev, staging and production, each mirrored as a demo running synthetic data
We’ll share more about the project and the partners behind it at interview.
## What you’ll do
* Lead the frontend: architecture, code quality, performance and releases.
* Set technical direction with the client and partner teams, and turn it into a plan.
* Build Thunk’s designs into map-led features — asset visualisation, prioritisation, export, onboarding.
* Integrate with partner APIs and GeoServer layers across all six environments.
* Own the release process in GitLab: reviews, tagged release candidates, production deploys.
* Keep the demo environments sharp for stakeholder presentations.
* Join user testing sessions, then fix what users show you.
* Pay down tech debt — starting with a smoother local setup — and keep the docs current.
### **Shaping how Thunk builds**
* Set our engineering standards: code review, testing, CI/CD and documentation.
* Lead technical scoping in discovery and pitches — approach, estimates, risks.
* Make infrastructure and tooling decisions, including how we run our own services.
* Explore where AI belongs in the products we build for clients.
* Mentor other developers, and help hire the next ones as we grow.
### **Across Thunk**
* Build prototypes for client discovery: real enough to test, quick enough to throw away.
* Contribute to Thunk’s own products, internal automation and website.
* Bring a developer’s view into early design and research: what’s feasible, quick or risky.
## **What you’ll bring**
* [5+] years building and shipping production software, ideally in a consultancy or agency.
* Strong React, Next.js and TypeScript, and modern CSS.
* A track record of owning projects end to end, from requirements to production.
* Experience integrating with APIs you don’t own — and raising clear issues when they break.
* CI/CD and infrastructure in practice: pipelines, multiple environments, infrastructure as code.
* Code and design review as habit. You raise the bar for the people around you.
* A feel for design.
* Accessibility as a default, not an afterthought.
* Clear, calm communication with clients and partners.

* Cloud platforms such as AWS, and Terraform or OpenTofu.

* Climate, infrastructure, utilities or public-sector projects.
* Mentoring developers or leading a small team.

We’re a small, remote-first team, allergic to consultant-speak and innovation theatre. We have hard earned values we stand by, we hope you will too. Feedback between the team is always direct rather than softened, because there’s no time for any other way. We care about craft over hype, and about the people behind the work more than the jargon we could wrap around it. We’re humanist technologists, so if you like humans AND technology you’ll fit right in. A dry sense of humour also helps.

# Regional Director of Operations, UK, Europe and Africa
* On-site
* + Bracknell, Bracknell Forest, United Kingdom
## Job description
**Regional Director of Operations, UK, Europe and Africa**
**Kenyon International Emergency Services, part of the TrustFlight Group**
Bracknell, United Kingdom | Full time, permanent | Competitive salary and benefits package
**When the worst happens, families need someone they can trust. Lead that response.**
When an aircraft is lost, a ship is in distress or a community is struck by disaster, families are suddenly facing the hardest days of their lives. They need answers, they need to be treated with dignity, and they need to know that the people they have lost are being cared for. For more than a century, Kenyon International Emergency Services has been the organisation that airlines, governments and major companies call on to make sure that happens.
We are looking for a senior crisis leader to direct that response across the UK, Europe and Africa. This is a role for someone who has stood in the room when it mattered, who leads with calm authority, and who believes that how an organisation treats the bereaved and the injured says everything about its character.
**About Kenyon**
Kenyon provides emergency planning, family assistance, humanitarian support and recovery services to clients around the world, drawing on a network of more than 2,500 trained responders who can be mobilised at short notice into any jurisdiction. Our clients rely on us to keep their promises to the people affected by an incident, and we hold ourselves to that standard every day, not only on the day of an activation.
Kenyon is part of the TrustFlight Group, an aviation safety and compliance technology business. That gives Kenyon something unusual in this sector: a world class technology team working alongside it, and a genuine commitment to using AI to make crisis response faster, better informed and more humane. Our values are simple and we mean them: integrity, and a customer first attitude in everything we do.
**The role**
Kenyon operates a two hub leadership model. You will lead the Bracknell hub, with regional accountability for operational delivery, readiness, contracted offices and relationships across the UK, Europe and Africa. Your peer, the Regional Director of Operations in Vancouver, leads the Americas and Asia Pacific. Together you share accountability for the readiness and quality of Kenyon’s response worldwide.
**Senior Incident Director for activations**
Senior on call duty is shared between the two Directors on a fixed twelve hour rota, with a structured handover at each change of duty, so that cover is continuous around the clock and neither Director works through their own night. Your window runs from approximately 06:00 to 18:00 UK time.
When an incident arises during your window, wherever in the world it occurs, you take up the role of Senior Incident Director. You will have the authority to set the deployment posture, commit responders and stand the organisation up or down without further approval. Where a client requires it, you will deploy as their strategic point of contact, leading the response on their behalf at the most demanding moments an organisation can face, including mass casualty, government led and politically sensitive events.
Major activations are infrequent, and Kenyon holds its capability through a surge based model rather than a large permanent workforce. Your judgement of regional readiness, kept current every week of the year, is what makes that model work.
**What you will lead**
· **Regional readiness and response.** Maintain and continuously measure activation readiness across the UK, Europe and Africa, and develop the procedures, protocols and contingency plans that underpin it.
· **Your team and offices.** Line manage the Regional Operations Manager in Bracknell, run the Bracknell hub and its regional operations as one regional function, and hold contracted offices to defined standards through quarterly reviews and an annual assessment.
· **Protecting those we serve.** Make sure the information of casualties, families and clients is protected with the same care during and after an activation as on any other day.
· **The responder network.** Work with the Responder Manager to keep the network vetted, trained and available across the region, including building language capable responders across Europe and Africa. Own the global standards for responder vetting, training currency, deployment conduct and post incident review, ensuring they are consistently applied across both hubs.
· **AI and digital quality assurance.** Work with the Vancouver Director and TrustFlight Group technology team to define and evaluate AI enabled quality and operational reporting tools, including an AI internal auditor supporting ISO 9001, ISO 27001 and ISO 22300 evidence gathering, gap identification and audit trail maintenance. Ensure these tools meet group information security, data governance and ethical standards.
· **Global operational standards.** Work with the Vancouver Director to compare regional procedures, share lessons learned and adopt improvements across both hubs, ensuring consistent service quality while recognising regional operational requirements.
· **Relationships that matter.** Build trusted working relationships with government agencies, emergency services, aviation authorities and clients across the region, and provide the operational insight that informs board level reporting.
**Why join us**
· **Work that matters.** Few roles offer the chance to lead a service whose sole purpose is to bring order, care and dignity to people at the worst moment of their lives.
· **Real authority.** A senior seat on the Kenyon leadership team, reporting to the Managing Director, with decision making authority during activations.
· **A sustainable model.** A shared rota designed so that no Director carries standing 24/7 availability, because sound judgement depends on rest.
· **Room to build.** The opportunity to shape Kenyon’s growth across the UK, Europe and Africa, while leading the development of global quality, certification and responder standards and helping shape how AI strengthens operational assurance across Kenyon.
In your cover letter, tell us about an incident you have led and what it taught you about caring for the people affected. Applications will be treated in strict confidence.
*Kenyon International Emergency Services and TrustFlight are equal opportunity employers. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and will make reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process for anyone who needs them. This position is employed by Kenyon International Emergency Services Limited.*
## Job requirements
**What you will bring**
· At least ten years in operational crisis management or emergency response, including five or more in a leadership role.
· Experience leading large scale or complex incident responses in international environments, ideally including direct responsibility for strategic command.
· A track record of managing contracted service providers against defined performance standards.
· Experience working within a quality management framework in a regulated or standards led environment, and alongside board level governance.
· The composure, judgement and compassion to lead when the stakes are highest, and the humility to put the needs of affected families first.
· Willingness to travel internationally at short notice, including to the United States and across Asia Pacific.
· Eligibility to live and work in the UK.
**It would be a real advantage if you also have**
· Professional fluency in Spanish, or another principal European and African language.
· Familiarity with the ISO 22300 series, including ISO 22320, or equivalent certification experience.
· Experience overseeing a 24/7 contact centre operation.
· Practical experience commissioning AI or automation tools in an operational setting.
· Knowledge of the aviation, maritime, energy or government crisis response markets in the Europe and Africa.

👋 Hello. Welcome to Wanstor! At Wanstor, we’ve been delivering award-winning IT solutions for over 22 years, and we’re proud to keep growing year after year. Today, our team is over 200 strong, filled with talented professionals passionate about technology.
Wanstor stands at the forefront of the industry with a full portfolio of high-quality services. From our award-winning managed services to our robust data and development capabilities, networking and infrastructure expertise, and unparalleled security solutions, Wanstor is renowned in the market for excellence. Our strong customer references provide a solid foundation for your success. If you’re looking for a place where your skills can thrive and grow, you’ll feel right at home here!
We’re looking for a Service Desk Analyst to join our Not for Profit team to work with one of our biggest customers in the charity sector. At Wanstor, our Service Desk Analysts are the heartbeat of our customer experience — the first voice, the first solution, and the first impression.
This role goes beyond answering calls and logging tickets — it’s about owning every challenge, delivering exceptional support, and making a real impact on the day-to-day operations of our customers.
## What You'll Do
· Responding to client’s technical issues via phone and email, triaging reported problems, resolving them, escalating them where necessary to more senior colleagues.
· Logging calls using service desk tools ITIL processes, working within these frameworks to deliver customer services levels >90% managing incidents to achieve where possible first call resolution and other company KPI’s.
· Maintaining good customer relations, including visiting sites within the greater London area.
· Managing user accounts within Office365 and allocating licenses.
· Managing Active Directory and Azure services including the creation of user accounts and amending permissions where needed.
· Using remote tools such as MDM, Remote control & Chat to resolve user requests.
· Deploying PC’s through Windows Autopilot and Intune.
· Setting up and configuring Windows based PCs and laptops.
## What You'll Need
You will have already started your journey within IT but are looking to develop your skills within a fast paced and supportive environment. You may have the following experience: -
* IT support experience at a 1st line level
* Knowledge of ITIL, incident, problem and change management.
* Experience taking responsibility and ownership of stakeholders and projects
* A desire to provide excellent, proactive, customer service
* Well organised, able to multitask and work autonomously
* Positive and energetic
* Happy to work a variety of shifts including weekends
## What You'll Love
🌴 **Generous Time Off:** Enjoy 24 days of annual leave, increasing by 1 day each year up to 28 days, plus Bank Holidays. 📚 **Continuous Learning:** Participate in regular lunch and learn sessions with both internal and external speakers. 🌟 **Personal Development:** Take advantage of 5 paid days annually to pursue new skills or knowledge. 🤝 **Volunteer Opportunities:** Contribute to your community with 2 paid volunteer days each year. 🎉 **Team Spirit:** Join a friendly team and engage in various social events organised throughout the year.
## About Wanstor
Wanstor is an award-winning IT Solutions Company celebrating its 22nd year in business. The company has grown year on year and now has a team of over 240 staff. With IT Support Offices in central London and regional field-based IT Support, we are well placed to meet our customers’ needs for a quick response.
We provide a range of hosted and deployed services for customers small and large. Our hosted solutions include hosted Email (Hosted Exchange), Hosted online back-up, Hosted Desktop, and Hosted Network Monitoring. Wanstor provides a full support service which includes a 24-hour helpdesk, network monitoring and on-site support. Wanstor’s clients provide a wide variety of fascinating opportunities for motivated technical staff. We employ service-oriented technical experts to work within our service team delivering a variety of hosted and deployed solutions.
We are a growing company with dedicated teams managing networks, storage and colocation. Our customers are some of the biggest brand names in the UK, and our consultants are some of the most skilled networking experts in the country.
As a service-centric organisation, we see people as our best competitive advantage as we strive to provide unsurpassed service to our customers. We expect a lot but at the same time are extremely supportive as we look to help realise each person’s potential in building a successful career with Wanstor.

* **For the changemakers**
For those who aren’t afraid to push boundaries and challenge the norm. Always one step ahead, we’re here to ignite innovation and propel businesses forward. We know that when tech runs flawlessly, everything else follows suit – giving our customers the space to pursue their next bold idea.

We analyse, critique, and execute with precision, knowing excellence lies in the details and true support means always showing up.
